<result># CLI Framework Research Report — create-pantoken-app

Research conducted via npm registry API, GitHub API (releases/commits/source), and web search, cross-checked against multiple sources. All dates relative to **today, August 27, 2026**.

---

## 1. citty (unjs/citty)

- **npm:** `citty`, latest **v0.2.2**, published **2026-04-01** (registry `modified` timestamp 2026-08-20, likely a metadata-only touch).
- **Downloads:** ~**30M/week** (huge, because it's a transitive dependency of Nuxt/nuxi, unbuild, and much of the UnJS ecosystem).
- **TypeScript/ESM:** Zero-dependency, TS-native, ESM-native. Built directly on Node's native `util.parseArgs` rather than a hand-rolled parser.
- **Command API** (verified from README):
```js
import { defineCommand, runMain } from "citty";
const main = defineCommand({
  meta: { name: "hello", version: "1.0.0", description: "My Awesome CLI App" },
  args: {
    name: { type: "positional", description: "Your name", required: true },
    friendly: { type: "boolean", description: "Use friendly greeting" },
  },
  setup({ args }) { /* pre-run hook */ },
  cleanup({ args }) { /* post-run hook, always runs */ },
  run({ args }) { console.log(`${args.friendly ? "Hi" : "Greetings"} ${args.name}!`); },
});
runMain(main);
```
Supports nested/lazy-loaded sub-commands, plugins (`defineCittyPlugin`), auto-generated `--help`/usage.
- **Shell completion:** **No built-in completion generator.** This is the one gap. However, the community project **`@bomb.sh/tab`** (see #9 below) ships a dedicated `citty.ts` adapter, giving citty bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell completions as a companion package. Not "batteries included," but a known, actively-maintained solution exists.

---

## 2. gunshi (kazupon/gunshi)

Confirmed **real and actively maintained** — not a mix-up with anything else.

- **npm:** `gunshi`, latest **v0.37.1**, released **2026-07-19** (dist-tags also show active `alpha`/`beta` channels, i.e., real ongoing release cadence).
- **Downloads:** ~**74K/week** for the core package — modest but healthy for a library only widely known since ~2024–2025. Real-world adopters include `ccusage` (a well-known Claude Code usage analyzer) and `varlock`.
- **TypeScript/ESM:** `"type": "module"` — **ESM-only**, no CJS. Runs on Node.js, Deno, and Bun. Type-safe args are powered by kazupon's own `args-tokens` parser.
- **Command API** (verified from README):
```js
import { cli } from 'gunshi'
const command = {
  name: 'greet',
  description: 'A greeting command',
  args: {
    name: { type: 'string', short: 'n', description: 'Name to greet' },
    times: { type: 'number', short: 't', default: 1, description: 'Repeat count' },
  },
  run: ctx => { /* ctx.values.name, ctx.values.times, fully typed */ }
}
await cli(process.argv.slice(2), command, { name: 'my-app', version: '1.0.0' })
```
- **Shell completions:** Yes — **`@gunshi/plugin-completion`** (part of the gunshi monorepo, versioned in lockstep), built on top of `@bomb.sh/tab`. This gives it a first-party, plugin-based completion story that citty/cac/commander lack natively. Weekly downloads for the plugin itself are small (~2.8K/week), consistent with an early but real adoption curve.
- **Caveat:** Explicitly inspired by/positioned as a successor to citty ("This project is inspired and powered by citty..."), with a heavier plugin architecture and internationalization built in. It's younger and smaller than citty/cac/commander — worth weighing "current and modern" against "less battle-tested at scale."

## 3. clipanion (Yarn Berry)

- **npm:** `clipanion`, latest dist-tag `latest` = **4.0.0-rc.4**.
- **Maintenance status: looks stale/stalled.** GitHub repo (`arcanis/clipanion`) last pushed **2024-09-06** — essentially **no commits in ~2 years** as of Aug 2026. 42 open issues, not archived, but no evidence of active development. The 4.0 release has been stuck in "rc" for two years.

- **TypeScript/ESM:** TypeScript-native (uses `typanion` for runtime validation), ships both CJS and ESM builds (`"main"` + `"module"` fields).

## 5. commander.js

- **npm:** `commander`, latest **v15.0.0**.

- **ESM/CJS:** Dual-mode, works fine under Node ESM.

## 6. oclif (Salesforce/Heroku)

- **Shell completion confirmed:** `@oclif/plugin-autocomplete` supports **bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell**, and remains the standard way big oclif-based CLIs ship completions.
- **ESM:** oclif has real ESM support as of the v3/v4 line — `oclif generate` lets you choose ESM or CommonJS at project creation, and ESM/CJS plugins can interoperate in the same CLI.
- **Heavyweight/opinionated verdict — confirmed true.** oclif is architected around **one class-per-command files** (`src/commands/<topic>/<command>.ts` each exporting a `Command` subclass), a plugin system, a generator/scaffolding CLI of its own, topic-based routing, and its own config/manifest conventions. This is the right tool when you're building a *many-subcommand* CLI (10s–100s of commands) that needs enterprise-grade plugin extensibility (exactly why Shopify/Twilio/Salesforce use it). For **your stated use case — a single main command (`create-pantoken-app <platform> [flags]`)** — oclif is disproportionately heavy: you'd be fighting its multi-file command-class model to express what is fundamentally one command with a positional argument and some flags. I would not recommend it here, despite it being extremely well-maintained.

---

## 7. @clack/prompts / @clack/core

- **npm:** both packages actively maintained; recent release cited as **v1.7.0** (~2 months prior to a late-2026 search snapshot) — consistent with steady, ongoing releases rather than abandonment.
- **Downloads:** ~**20.45M/week** for `@clack/prompts`, ~**20.4M/week** for `@clack/core` — extremely high adoption, on par with commander-level ubiquity for the "interactive prompts" niche specifically.
- **Confirmed real-world scaffolder usage (verified via each project's actual npm dependencies, not just claims):**
  - **`create-t3-app`** and **`create-next-app`** — commonly cited as clack adopters.
  - **`sv` (the new Svelte CLI, replacing `create-svelte`)** — **confirmed directly from source**: `packages/sv/package.json` depends on `@clack/prompts` (v1.5.0) for prompts and **`commander`** (^15.0.0) for command/arg structure. This is a clean, current example of exactly the split-responsibility pattern you're asking about.
  - **`shadcn` CLI** — I checked this one specifically because it's often *assumed* to use clack, but as of **v4.19.0** its actual npm dependencies show it uses the older **`prompts`** (terkelg's library, ^2.4.2) alongside commander — **not** `@clack/prompts`. Worth correcting: don't assume shadcn as a clack reference implementation.
  - **`create-astro`** — I also checked this directly: it depends on `@astrojs/cli-kit` (Astro's own bespoke prompt library, built from `chalk` + `log-update` + `sisteransi` primitives), **not** `@clack/prompts`. A GitHub Actions log title referencing "switch to clack for CLI prompts" turned up in search but doesn't match what's actually in `@astrojs/cli-kit`'s or `create-astro`'s published dependencies — I could not confirm that claim and am flagging it as unverified/likely referring to a different Astro subsystem.
  - **`create-vue`** and **`drizzle-kit`** — could not verify their prompt libraries directly from public dependency manifests in the time available. Note: the Drizzle team has publicly said they built their own **`hanji`** library (after trying `ink`) rather than adopting clack, so treat "drizzle-kit uses clack" as **unconfirmed/likely false** rather than fact.
- **Net assessment:** `@clack/prompts` is healthy, current, and one of two or three real leaders in this space in 2026, but it is **not universally used** by every well-known scaffolder — some (shadcn, Astro, Drizzle) roll their own or use older libraries. Treat "everyone uses clack" as directionally true but not literally true.

---

## 8. What bingo (create.bingo, Josh Goldberg) uses for its own CLI

I inspected the actual `bingo-js/bingo` monorepo source (not just docs, which don't state this explicitly):

- The core **`bingo`** package (the runtime that powers `npx create-typescript-app`-style CLIs) depends directly on **`@clack/prompts` (^0.11.0)** for its interactive prompt layer, plus `zod` (^4.4.3) for schema validation of inputs.
- For argument parsing, bingo does **not** depend on citty/cac/commander/oclif/gunshi at all — it hand-rolls its own minimal parser (`src/cli/parseProcessArgv.ts`, `src/cli/cliArgsOptions.ts` in the `bingo` package). There's no evidence bingo has a stated "opinion" recommending a specific arg-parser to pair with it; it just uses the simplest thing that works for its own needs.
- Note: the `create` package on npm (the literal package named `create`) is **not** the real scaffolding logic — it's a decoy/trap package that just prints a warning telling people they meant `npm create <template>` instead of `npx create`. Don't confuse it with bingo's actual CLI runtime.
- **Implication for pantoken:** bingo itself validates the "commander/citty/cac + clack" split pattern from the inside — its own author independently chose `@clack/prompts` for prompting rather than any all-in-one framework, while keeping arg-parsing bespoke and minimal (which for bingo's needs is fine, but for a public `npx create-pantoken-app` CLI with `--help`/completions requirements, you'd still want a real parser library rather than replicating bingo's hand-rolled approach).

---

## 9. The actual 2026 pattern: split arg-parsing from prompting

Confirmed directly from source across three real, current scaffolders — this is not just a general impression, it's what's actually in their `package.json`s:

|---|---|---|
| **`sv` (Svelte CLI)** | `commander` ^15.0.0 | `@clack/prompts` 1.5.0 |
| **`shadcn` CLI** | `commander` ^14.0.0 | `prompts` ^2.4.2 (not clack) |
| **`create-astro`** | bespoke (`@astrojs/cli-kit`, giget for cloning) | bespoke, built on chalk/log-update/sisteransi (not clack) |
| **bingo (create.bingo)** | bespoke minimal parser | `@clack/prompts` ^0.11.0 |

**Conclusion: yes, the dominant modern pattern is a lightweight arg-parser paired with a separate prompts library — not a single all-in-one framework like oclif** — but *which* prompt library varies (clack is popular but not unanimous; commander is the most common arg-parser among these, more so than citty/cac in this particular sample).

The most concrete new 2026 development for **completions specifically** is **`@bomb.sh/tab`** (`@bomb.sh/tab` on npm, ~1.5M downloads/week, latest release **v0.0.22 on 2026-08-04** — actively maintained, pre-1.0 but broadly adopted). It's a shell-completion engine, independent of any one arg-parser, that ships first-party adapters for **citty, cac, and commander** (confirmed by inspecting its source tree: `src/cac.ts`, `src/citty.ts`, `src/commander.ts`) plus native generators for **bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell** (confirmed from its README: "autocompletions that work consistently across zsh, bash, fish, and powershell"). It's also the engine underneath `@gunshi/plugin-completion`. Its README lists Cloudflare, Nuxt, Astro, Vitest, Gunshi, Clerc, and Prisma as adopters. This effectively **solves the "citty/cac/commander have no built-in completions" gap** for you without needing oclif's heavier framework just to get `@oclif/plugin-autocomplete`.

I've now verified Crust directly: its core package (`@crustjs/core`) is explicitly Bun-native — the getting-started flow is `bun create crust`, and nothing in its README indicates Node.js support. That's disqualifying here: `npx create-pantoken-app` has to work for any npm/Node user, and requiring a Bun runtime would break that on any machine without Bun installed. I'll note it in the plan as considered-and-rejected with that reasoning, rather than as a viable option.

Here's the full comparison I've now verified (npm registry + GitHub, checked against real scaffolders' actual dependencies, not just marketing pages):

| Library | Role | 2026 health | Completions | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **citty** | arg-parsing/help | v0.2.2, ~30M dl/wk, zero-dep, powers Nuxt CLI | via `@bomb.sh/tab` adapter | Strong candidate |
| **commander** | arg-parsing/help | v15.0.0, ~505M dl/wk, safest/most proven | via `@bomb.sh/tab` adapter | Strong candidate |
| gunshi | arg-parsing/help | v0.37.1, ~74K dl/wk, younger | built-in plugin (on `@bomb.sh/tab`) | Viable but less battle-tested |
| clipanion | arg-parsing/help | no commits since 2024-09 | none | Stale — reject |
| oclif | full framework | v4.24.0, very healthy | built-in, all shells | Over-architected for one command — reject |
| **@clack/prompts** | interactive prompts | ~20M dl/wk, healthy | — | Recommended — already a transitive dep here via bingo-stratum and `@changesets/cli` |
| **@bomb.sh/tab** | completions engine | v0.0.22, pre-1.0 but adopted by Nuxt/Astro/Vitest/Prisma | bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell | Recommended, only real cross-parser answer |
| Crust | full framework | Bun-only | via plugin | **Rejected — requires Bun runtime** |

The concrete, verified real-world pattern for exactly this kind of tool — a single scaffolding command with a framework/platform picker — is Svelte's `sv` CLI: `commander` + `@clack/prompts`. That's about as close an analog to `create-pantoken-app` as exists. citty is the other serious option: zero-dependency, native to `util.parseArgs`, and stylistically closer to the Vite/oxc-flavored tooling pantoken already leans on (vite-plus, oxlint, oxfmt).

I have two fork decisions before I finalize the plan:

### 1. @inquirer/prompts — healthy and actively maintained.

- **Version:** 8.7.0 (dist-tag `latest`), published **2026-08-26** — one day before this report.

- **ESM/TS status:** ESM-native since v9, and each prompt ships as its own scoped package (`@inquirer/select`, `@inquirer/checkbox`, `@inquirer/confirm`, etc.), all built on `@inquirer/core` (currently v12.0.1). TypeScript types are first-class.
- **Visual style:** More traditional than clack's connected vertical-line aesthetic. It uses arrows, checkmarks, and inline highlighting, and supports theming through a theme object, but it doesn't group steps into a single visual "flow" the way clack does out of the box. Expect to do more manual styling if you want clack's polished, boxed look.
- **Spinner:** No built-in spinner or progress primitive. The common pairing is `ora`, which the ecosystem treats as a known, well-tested combination (though there have been historical stdio-conflict bugs between ora and inquirer that got resolved).
- **Ctrl+C/cancellation:** Rejects the prompt's promise on Ctrl+C by design, so your code can clean up before exiting. It also supports an `AbortController`/`signal` option for programmatic cancellation. There are a few open GitHub issues about a delay before the rejection fires on `@inquirer/select` and about nested-prompt Ctrl+C edge cases, but the overall model is deliberate and documented, not the silent, do-nothing behavior classic `inquirer` was criticized for.
- **Real-world use:** It's the direct successor to the original `inquirer`, which itself has an enormous install base going back to Yeoman-era tooling. The modern package is newer to broad scaffolder adoption than clack, but it's the default choice for anyone staying inside the Inquirer ecosystem.

- **Downloads:** ~59.6M/week — the highest raw number of the four, but this is a lagging indicator. It reflects legacy transitive dependencies pinned by older tools, not fresh adoption. - **Ctrl+C handling:** This is the exact pain point you're trying to avoid. By default, pressing Ctrl+C on a confirm prompt answers "yes" and continues execution instead of aborting — you have to wire up a custom `onCancel` callback to get sane behavior. There's an open, unresolved GitHub issue asking for this default to change.
- **Spinner:** None built in.
- **Verdict:** Stale, with real UX foot-guns baked into the defaults. Not a good choice for a new scaffolding CLI in 2026.

### 3. enquirer — rule it out; more stale than prompts.

- **Version:** 2.4.1, last published **2023-07-28** — over three years ago.
- **Repo activity:** Last GitHub push was **2024-06-11**, over two years before this report. 207 open issues sit untouched. This confirms your recollection: the historical maintenance gaps have continued, and the project now looks effectively dormant.

## Background

pantoken has three independently hand-rolled argv parsers, all with no real help system, no shell completions, and thin/inconsistent interactivity:

1. **`packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts`** (`runScaffoldCli`, `shouldPromptForDir`) — the canonical shared CLI, consumed by both:

   Current contract (read the full file — it's short): manual `parseArgs` loop, one required positional `<platform>`, `--dir <path>`, `--help`/`-h`; throws `Unknown option "..."` on anything else. Directory is prompted via raw `node:readline/promises` ONLY when `--dir` is omitted AND `process.stdin.isTTY === true` (helper `shouldPromptForDir`); otherwise defaults silently to `"."`. No platform prompt at all — omitting the platform just errors. `scaffoldProject()` (in `packages/scaffold/src/index.ts`) is the underlying platform→files function; treat it as a stable API, do not redesign it (it already handles Bingo-preset rendering with a legacy string-template fallback — that's a separate, pre-existing concern, out of scope here).

2. **`ai/pantoken-ai/bin/pantoken-ai.mjs`** — a second, fully separate hand-rolled parser with its own `init`/`scaffold <platform>` subcommands and a `--tool <name>` flag (values from `AGENT_TOOLS` in `ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts`, or `"all"`). It does NOT reuse `packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts` at all — it only imports `scaffoldAndInit`/`installAgentAssets`/`isScaffoldPlatform`/`SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS`/`AGENT_TOOLS` from `../dist/index.mjs`. 3. `packages/cli` (`@pantoken/cli`, the native-token `pantoken generate <target>` CLI) is a THIRD hand-rolled parser but is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — different domain (native token generation, not scaffolding), do not touch it or mention consolidating it.

Preserve the EXACT existing default-behavior contract for non-interactive/CI use: when `--dir` is given OR stdin is not a TTY, do NOT prompt — same for platform: if platform is given as a positional, don't prompt for it either. - **Shell completions: `@bomb.sh/tab`** — a completions engine (pre-1.0, v0.0.22, but adopted by Nuxt/Astro/Vitest/Prisma) with a first-party `commander` adapter (confirmed to exist in its source tree as `src/commander.ts`, generating bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell completions). ---

## Phase 1 — Rewrite `packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts`

Replace the manual `parseArgs` loop with a commander-based command builder, exporting granular, independently reusable pieces (not just one opaque function), so `ai/pantoken-ai/src/cli.ts` can compose its own subcommand from the same logic instead of reimplementing it or wrapping an entire pre-built `Command`.

### New exports from `packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts`

```ts
// Re-exported for convenience so cli.ts consumers need one import, not two.
export { SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS, isScaffoldPlatform } from "./index.ts";

/** Thrown for user-facing CLI errors (missing platform under --yes, etc.); carries an exit code. */
export class ScaffoldCliError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, public readonly exitCode: number = 1) { super(message); }
}

/** Whether a value should be interactively prompted for: no flag/arg given, not --yes, and stdin is a TTY. */
export function shouldPrompt(value: string | undefined, opts: { yes?: boolean; isTTY?: boolean }): boolean;

export interface ResolveScaffoldTargetOptions {
  platformArg?: string;
  dirOption?: string;
  yes?: boolean;
  /** Injectable for tests; defaults to `process.stdin.isTTY`. */
  isTTY?: boolean;
}

/**
 * Resolve platform + directory: validates/prompts for platform via clack `select()` when omitted
 * on a TTY (not --yes); validates/prompts for dir via clack `text()` under the same conditions;
 * throws ScaffoldCliError with a clear message when a required value is missing non-interactively.
 */
export async function resolveScaffoldTarget(
  options: ResolveScaffoldTargetOptions,
): Promise<{ platform: ScaffoldPlatform; dir: string }>;

/** Runs `scaffoldProject()` wrapped in a clack `spinner()`; returns the written paths. */
export async function scaffoldWithSpinner(platform: ScaffoldPlatform, dir: string): Promise<string[]>;

/** Detects the invoking package manager from `npm_config_user_agent` (create-vite/create-vue technique). */
export function detectPackageManager(
  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
): "npm" | "pnpm" | "yarn" | "bun" | undefined;

/** Prints the post-scaffold "Next steps" block. See Phase 1a for the exact text/behavior decision. */
export function printNextSteps(dir: string, written: string[]): void;

/** A commander `Argument` validator for the platform positional, shared by both CLIs. */
export function validateScaffoldPlatform(value: string): string; // throws commander.InvalidArgumentError

export interface ScaffoldCommandOptions {
  /** Program name shown in help/usage. Default: "pantoken-scaffold". */
  name?: string;
  /** Exact invocation string for help examples, e.g. "npm create pantoken-app --". Defaults to `name`. */
  usageCommand?: string;
  /** Version string for `--version`. No default — callers pass their own package.json version. */
  version?: string;
  /**
   * Whether to auto-register @bomb.sh/tab completion subcommands on this Command. Default: true.
   * Set false only if this Command will be mounted as a subcommand of a larger root program that
   * wires completions itself (not used by the current design — see Phase 4 — but kept for flexibility).
   */
  enableCompletions?: boolean;
}

/** Builds the full, ready-to-parse commander Command for `pantoken-scaffold`/`create-pantoken-app`. */
export function createScaffoldCommand(options?: ScaffoldCommandOptions): Command;

/** Back-compat wrapper preserving the old call shape, now implemented via createScaffoldCommand(). */
export async function runScaffoldCli(
  argv: string[],
  options: { usageCommand: string; version?: string },
): Promise<void>;
```

Note: `shouldPromptForDir` is removed (renamed/generalized to `shouldPrompt`, now used for both platform and dir); this is the one deliberate breaking rename to a previously-exported-and-tested symbol, called out explicitly in the changeset and the test rewrite (Phase 5).

### `createScaffoldCommand()` shape (commander v15 + `@commander-js/extra-typings`)

```ts
import { Argument, InvalidArgumentError, CommanderError } from "commander";
import { Command } from "@commander-js/extra-typings";
import tab from "@bomb.sh/tab/commander";

const program = new Command(options?.name ?? "pantoken-scaffold")
  .exitOverride()                       // throw CommanderError instead of calling process.exit
  .configureOutput({ writeOut: (s) => process.stdout.write(s), writeErr: (s) => process.stderr.write(s) })
  .addArgument(new Argument("[platform]", `Platform to scaffold (${SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join("|")}; "html" is an alias for "components")`).argParser(validateScaffoldPlatform))
  .option("-d, --dir <path>", "Target directory (defaults to \".\"; prompts interactively on a TTY if omitted)")
  .option("-y, --yes", "Never prompt; fail with an error instead of prompting for a missing platform or directory", false);

if (options?.version) program.version(options.version, "-v, --version");

program.action(async (platformArg, opts) => {
  const { platform, dir } = await resolveScaffoldTarget({ platformArg, dirOption: opts.dir, yes: opts.yes });
  const written = await scaffoldWithSpinner(platform, dir);
  for (const path of written) console.log(`✓ wrote ${path}`);
  printNextSteps(dir, written);
});

if (options?.enableCompletions ?? true) tab(program, { completionCommandName: "completion" });
return program;
```

Key precision points:
- **Platform validation happens at commander's argument-parse layer** via `validateScaffoldPlatform` (an `Argument.argParser`), not `.choices()` — `.choices()` can't be used because `isScaffoldPlatform("html")` must pass even though `"html"` is an alias not in `SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS`. The validator message becomes commander's own `error: command-argument value '...' is invalid for argument 'platform'. <our message>` format — this is a real, user-visible wording change from today's `Unknown platform "...".` (see Phase 5 for the test-contract implication).
- **A second stray positional (e.g. `pantoken-scaffold react extra`) is now rejected by commander itself** ("too many arguments") since only one `[platform]` argument is declared — replaces the old `Unknown option "extra".` message with commander's own wording. This is a deliberate, acceptable behavior change (still fails clearly, just different text).
- **`.exitOverride()` + `.configureOutput()`** is the standard, well-documented commander pattern for making a Command safe to `parseAsync()` from a library context and for unit-testing without a real `process.exit` — it throws `CommanderError` (carrying `.exitCode` and `.code`, e.g. `"commander.helpDisplayed"`, `"commander.version"`, `"commander.invalidArgument"`) instead of exiting or bypassing mocked I/O.
- **`--yes`/`-y`**: forces `resolveScaffoldTarget` to skip both prompts; if platform is still missing, it throws `ScaffoldCliError('Missing required argument "platform". Expected one of: ...')`, which the caller (`runScaffoldCli`, see below) reports the same way as any other user-facing error.

### `resolveScaffoldTarget` internals (the reusable prompt flow)

- Platform: if `platformArg` is given, it's already been validated by commander's argParser by the time this runs (when called from `createScaffoldCommand`); when called from `ai/pantoken-ai`'s own hand-built subcommand (Phase 4), `resolveScaffoldTarget` must **also** validate an unvalidated `platformArg` itself (since that caller may not run it through commander's argParser) — so `resolveScaffoldTarget` should call `isScaffoldPlatform`/throw its own `ScaffoldCliError` defensively even if the argument theoretically arrives pre-validated. This makes it safe to call from either context.
- If `platformArg` is omitted:
  - `shouldPrompt(platformArg, { yes, isTTY })` false → throw `ScaffoldCliError` (missing platform, non-interactive).
  - true → `@clack/prompts` `select({ message: "Which platform?", options: SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.map((p) => ({ value: p, label: p })) })`. On `isCancel(result)` → `cancel("Cancelled.")`, throw `ScaffoldCliError("Cancelled.", 1)`.
- Directory: same `shouldPrompt` gate; on true, `text({ message: "Project directory", placeholder: ".", defaultValue: "." })` (clack returns the default automatically on empty Enter — replaces the old manual `.trim() || "."`). Same cancel handling.
- On `--yes` with `--dir` omitted: silently defaults to `"."` (unchanged from today's non-TTY default) — `--yes` does **not** require `--dir`, only `platform`.

### 1a. The "next steps" / package-manager-detection fork — **flagging for your decision**

**Finding:** the scaffolded projects' generated `package.json` files (checked `packages/scaffold/generated/scaffolds.ts`) never depend on `vite-plus`/`vp` — `vp install` is pantoken's own convention recommendation, not something tied to the scaffolded project itself. Today's message is a static string:
```
Next steps:
  cd <dir>
  vp install   (or npm/pnpm/yarn/bun install)
```
**Finding (test-breaking risk):** `packages/create-pantoken-app/tests/index.test.ts` and `packages/scaffold/tests/cli.test.ts` both assert `output.toContain("vp install")` on the output of the **spawned child-process bin**, run under this monorepo's own pnpm-driven test runner — meaning `process.env.npm_config_user_agent` is already set to `pnpm/...` for that child process. If `detectPackageManager()` is used to *replace* the printed line, these tests would see `"pnpm install"` instead and fail.

Two options — **recommend Option A as the default; Option B needs explicit sign-off** since it changes visible output and requires updating 3 existing test assertions:
- **Option A (recommended, zero test breakage):** implement `detectPackageManager()` and export it, but do **not** wire it into `printNextSteps()`'s primary line yet. Keep printing the exact current static text. This satisfies "investigate" without a behavior change; `detectPackageManager` becomes available for `ai/pantoken-ai` or a later follow-up to use.
- **Option B (behavior change):** `printNextSteps` prints `${detectPackageManager() ?? "vp"} install` as the primary line, falling back to today's full static text only when detection fails. Requires updating the two "vp install" assertions in `packages/scaffold/tests/cli.test.ts` and one in `packages/create-pantoken-app/tests/index.test.ts` to either force-clear `npm_config_user_agent` in the test's `env` before spawning, or assert `/install/` instead of the literal string.

Plan proceeds with **Option A**; flip to Option B only if you confirm you want the behavior change.

### Backward-compatible `runScaffoldCli`

```ts
export async function runScaffoldCli(argv: string[], options: { usageCommand: string; version?: string }) {
  const program = createScaffoldCommand({ name: options.usageCommand, usageCommand: options.usageCommand, version: options.version });
  try {
    await program.parseAsync(argv, { from: "user" });
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof CommanderError) {
      if (err.code === "commander.helpDisplayed" || err.code === "commander.version") return; // matches old "--help returns without exiting" contract
      process.exit(err.exitCode);
    }
    if (err instanceof ScaffoldCliError) {
      console.error(err.message);
      process.exit(err.exitCode);
    }
    console.error("Error scaffolding project:", err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```
This is what both `packages/scaffold/bin/pantoken-scaffold.mjs` and `packages/create-pantoken-app/bin/create-pantoken-app.mjs` continue to call — **both bin files need zero or near-zero changes**. The only optional addition: pass a `version` read from each package's own `package.json` via `import pkg from "../package.json" with { type: "json" }` (Node 22 JSON import attributes — safe given `engines.node >=22.18.0`), so `--version` reports the correct package version per binary.

---

## Phase 2 — `packages/scaffold/bin/pantoken-scaffold.mjs`

Minimal change (adds `--version` support, otherwise identical):
```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { runScaffoldCli } from "../dist/cli.mjs";
import pkg from "../package.json" with { type: "json" };

await runScaffoldCli(process.argv.slice(2), { usageCommand: "pantoken-scaffold", version: pkg.version });
```

## Phase 3 — `packages/create-pantoken-app/bin/create-pantoken-app.mjs`

Same pattern, its own package.json version:
```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { runScaffoldCli } from "@pantoken/scaffold/cli";
import pkg from "../package.json" with { type: "json" };

await runScaffoldCli(process.argv.slice(2), {
  usageCommand: "npm create pantoken-app --",
  version: pkg.version,
});
```
`npx create-pantoken-app <platform> [--dir]` and `npm create pantoken-app -- <platform>` keep working unchanged; they also transparently gain `--yes`, prompts, and completions via the shared `runScaffoldCli`.

---

## Phase 4 — `ai/pantoken-ai` consolidation

**Finding:** `ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts` has **no CLI-parsing tests at all** — only library-level tests of `installAgentAssets`/`scaffoldAndInit`/`scaffoldProject`. This means the `bin/pantoken-ai.mjs` argv contract is unlocked by tests today, giving full freedom to redesign it (still worth adding new tests, per Phase 5).

### New file: `ai/pantoken-ai/src/cli.ts`

Mirrors `packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts`'s pattern: exports a builder + a run wrapper.

```ts
export interface AiCommandOptions { name?: string; version?: string }

export function createAiCommand(options?: AiCommandOptions): Command {
  const program = new Command(options?.name ?? "pantoken-ai")
    .exitOverride()
    .configureOutput({ writeOut: (s) => process.stdout.write(s), writeErr: (s) => process.stderr.write(s) });
  if (options?.version) program.version(options.version, "-v, --version");

  program
    .command("init")
    .description("Write pantoken's agent assets into a repo")
    .addOption(new Option("-t, --tool <tool>", `Tool (${["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS].join("|")})`).default("all").choices(["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS]))
    .option("-d, --dir <path>", "Target directory", ".")
    .action((opts) => {
      const written = installAgentAssets(opts.tool, opts.dir);
      for (const p of written) console.log(`✓ wrote ${p}`);
    });

  program
    .command("scaffold")
    .description("Scaffold a starter project (via @pantoken/scaffold) and install agent assets into the same directory")
    .addArgument(new Argument("[platform]", `Platform (${SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join("|")})`).argParser(validateScaffoldPlatform))
    .option("-d, --dir <path>", "Target directory (prompts interactively on a TTY if omitted)")
    .option("-y, --yes", "Never prompt", false)
    .addOption(new Option("-t, --tool <tool>", `Agent tool (${["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS].join("|")})`).default("all").choices(["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS]))
    .action(async (platformArg, opts) => {
      const { platform, dir } = await resolveScaffoldTarget({ platformArg, dirOption: opts.dir, yes: opts.yes });
      const scaffoldFiles = await scaffoldWithSpinner(platform, dir);
      const assetFiles = installAgentAssets(opts.tool, dir);
      for (const p of [...scaffoldFiles, ...assetFiles]) console.log(`✓ wrote ${p}`);
      printNextSteps(dir, scaffoldFiles);
    });

  tab(program, { completionCommandName: "completion" }); // wired once, on this program's own root
  return program;
}

export async function runAiCli(argv: string[], options?: AiCommandOptions): Promise<void> {
  // same exitOverride/CommanderError/ScaffoldCliError catch pattern as runScaffoldCli
}
```

- Note the `scaffold` command here uses `.command("scaffold")` + a manually attached `Argument` (rather than the string-shorthand `.command("scaffold <platform>")`) specifically so `validateScaffoldPlatform` (imported from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`) can be attached via `.argParser`, keeping a single source of truth for the platform-validation error message across all three CLIs.
- `resolveScaffoldTarget`, `scaffoldWithSpinner`, `printNextSteps`, `validateScaffoldPlatform` are all imported from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli` — this is the literal reuse the task calls for: the platform-select/dir-text/spinner UI runs unmodified, then `installAgentAssets` runs after.
- `printNextSteps` is now shared verbatim across all three CLIs, which changes `pantoken-ai scaffold`'s old output from `"\nNext: cd ${dir} && npm install (or pnpm/yarn/bun install)"` to the same `"Next steps:\n  cd ...\n  vp install ..."` block used by `pantoken-scaffold`. **This is a deliberate, user-visible behavior change for `@pantoken/ai`**, worth its own line in that package's changeset.
- Completions (`tab(program, ...)`) are wired **exactly once**, on `ai/pantoken-ai`'s own root `Command`, covering both its `init` and `scaffold` subcommands. `createScaffoldCommand()` (from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`) is deliberately **not** mounted wholesale here via `addCommand()` — reusing granular functions instead avoids double-registering a nested `completion` subcommand and gives room for the `--tool` option that `createScaffoldCommand()` doesn't know about.

### `ai/pantoken-ai/bin/pantoken-ai.mjs` — becomes a thin shim

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { runAiCli } from "../dist/cli.mjs";
import pkg from "../package.json" with { type: "json" };

await runAiCli(process.argv.slice(2), { version: pkg.version });
```
This matches `packages/scaffold/bin/pantoken-scaffold.mjs`'s bin/src split convention exactly, as required.

## Phase 5 — Test rewrite plan

### `packages/scaffold/tests/cli.test.ts` — rewrite, new assertions

- Drop the `readline/promises` mocking block entirely; replace with `vi.doMock("@clack/prompts", () => ({ select: vi.fn(), text: vi.fn(), spinner: () => ({ start: vi.fn(), stop: vi.fn() }), isCancel: () => false, cancel: vi.fn() }))`, same `vi.resetModules()` + fresh dynamic `import("../src/cli.ts")` pattern already used today for the readline mock — same mechanics, different module.

- Replace `'Unknown option "extra".'` (second positional) with: assert non-zero exit and stderr contains `"too many arguments"`.
- Replace `'Unknown platform "not-a-real-platform".'` with: assert non-zero exit and stderr contains both `"not-a-real-platform"` and `"platform"`.

# @bomb.sh/tty

A low-level, platform-independent terminal renderer and event parser for
JavaScript. You can use `@bomb.sh/tty` directly, or as the foundation for your
own framework.

## Features

**Declarative terminal UI** — Build terminal interfaces the same way you'd build
a web page. `@bomb.sh/tty` uses [Clay](https://github.com/nicbarker/clay) under
the hood, giving you flexbox-like layout, pointer detection, and scroll
containers — all rendered to the terminal as box-drawing characters and ANSI
escape sequences.

**Zero I/O** — `@bomb.sh/tty` never reads stdin or writes stdout. You feed it
bytes and get bytes back. This makes it trivially embeddable in any framework,
any runtime, any event loop. There are no opinions about how you do I/O, just
pure computation.

**Runs everywhere** — The entire engine is compiled to WebAssembly, so
`@bomb.sh/tty` will run anywhere JavaScript runs with no native dependencies,
and no build step for consumers.

### Examples

See this keyboard example and more in the [examples folder](examples/README.md).
This demo uses `@bomb.sh/tty` for all layout and input parsing.

#### Keyboard Events

The input parser decodes raw terminal bytes into structured events. Here you can
see each key event as the string "hello world" is typed.

#### Pointer Events

Here we see hover styles applied to UI elements in response to the pointer
state. Clay drives the hit testing; no manual coordinate math required.

![Pointer events demo](examples/keyboard/keyboard-pointer-events.gif)

## Architecture

`@bomb.sh/tty` does not do any I/O itself. On the ouput side, it converts UI
elements into a raw sequence of bytes and pointer events, and on the input side,
it converts a stream of raw bytes into structured events.

to WASM in a single call. On the C side, Clay runs layout, render commands are

Findings on both:

- **`@bomb.sh/args`** — a real package (v0.3.1, published Feb 2025, ~11K downloads/week), but it's a minimal (<1kB) flag-only parser with no subcommands, no auto-generated `--help`, and no choices/enum validation. Confirmed it isn't even in `@bomb.sh/tab`'s own adapter list (tab only ships adapters for cac, citty, and commander) — so pairing it with tab would mean writing a custom, unproven adapter ourselves. It can't do what commander does here (subcommands, typed choices, generated help).
- **`@bomb.sh/tty`** — exists (v0.8.0, created June 2026, only ~93 downloads/week) but it's a completely different kind of tool: a low-level, zero-I/O, WASM-compiled terminal *rendering engine* (flexbox-style layout via Clay) meant as a foundation for building full interactive TUI frameworks — not a prompts library. Adopting it for a platform/directory prompt wizard would be significant overkill for what's needed here.

Neither improves on the existing commander + `@clack/prompts` + `@bomb.sh/tab` stack for this use case, so I'm keeping that recommendation. Updating the plan with this research plus the branch/commit workflow now.

## Branch and commit workflow

Work happens on a new feature branch off `main` (e.g. `feat/scaffold-cli-commander-clack`), not directly
on `main`. Commit incrementally per phase using this repo's existing conventional-commit style (confirmed
from git history: `feat(scope): ...`, `fix(scope): ...`, `test(scope): ...`, `docs(scope): ...`,
`chore(scope): ...`), pushing the branch after each commit so progress is visible, then opening a pull
request once the full plan is implemented and verified:

1. `chore(scaffold): add commander, @clack/prompts, and @bomb.sh/tab to the catalog` — Phase 0.
2. `feat(scaffold): rebuild the shared CLI on commander and @clack/prompts` — Phase 1 + the
   `packages/scaffold/tests/cli.test.ts` rewrite from Phase 5 (keep implementation and its own tests in the
   same commit so `vp test` stays green at each step).
3. `feat(create-pantoken-app): pass --version through to the shared CLI` — Phase 2–3 (small; could also
   fold into commit 2 if trivial enough once written).

One more important finding: `@pantoken/i18n`'s runtime API (`registerLocalized`, `LocaleBundle`) is tightly coupled to `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom-element registration — its `strings` type is fixed to web-components' specific keys, not a generic message catalog. So it can't be used as-is for arbitrary CLI strings without modifying a shared, already-published package's public API. The genuinely reusable piece is one layer lower: `tools/translation-adapters` (the `claude`/`agy`-CLI-spawning adapter + committed-cache mechanism that both docs and `@pantoken/i18n` build on) — that's generic and safe to reuse directly.

Given that, I'd recommend a small scaffold-local i18n slice (its own `src/i18n.json`, its own committed cache, its own codegen into `generated/locales/*.ts`) built on that shared low-level adapter, rather than reaching into and generalizing `@pantoken/i18n`'s web-components-specific API. Two scope questions before I fold this into the plan:

questions.question: How many locales should the CLI's translated strings target initially? Real AI translation requires a human to run a manual `claude`/`agy` CLI step locally (same as docs' existing workflow) — it's not automatic in CI.

options.label: Ship detection + English only now (Recommended)
options.description: Build the locale-detection + t()-lookup infrastructure with graceful English fallback, and commit only the English source strings. Translating into other languages becomes a fast, separate follow-up (just run the translate script) once the CLI strings are finalized — avoids translating prose that's still likely to change during this rewrite.

options.label: Match docs' locale set now (en + hu)
options.description: Also run the manual translate step for Hungarian as part of this change, matching the docs site's current language support exactly.

This also consolidates `ai/pantoken-ai`'s separate hand-rolled `init`/`scaffold` CLI onto the same engine,
per this repo's own convention of updating `@pantoken/ai` alongside user-facing scaffold changes so
guidance doesn't drift — reducing three duplicate parsers to one shared foundation.

This is a clean rewrite, not a backward-compatible refactor: the old argv contract, exact error-message
wording, and internal exports (`shouldPromptForDir`, etc.) are not preserved. Every affected package's
changeset is a `major` bump, calling out the behavior change plainly rather than papering over it with a
compat shim.

The CLI's own prose (prompts, help text, error messages, next-steps output) is also localized: the CLI
detects the invoking terminal's language and shows translated strings where available, falling back to
English. This reuses `@pantoken/translation-adapters` — the generic, already-existing low-level piece
(`spawnPrompt`, `TranslationMemory`) that both the docs site and `@pantoken/i18n` build their own
translation pipelines on — rather than `@pantoken/i18n` itself, whose public runtime API
(`registerLocalized`, `LocaleBundle`) is tightly coupled to `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom-element
registration and isn't a generic message catalog. See Phase 0.5.

For localization, **`@pantoken/translation-adapters`** (`tools/translation-adapters`, exports `TranslationMemory`,
`spawnPrompt`, `sha256`) is reused directly — it's the generic adapter-spawning/caching core, with no
markdown or web-components coupling. `@pantoken/i18n` (`packages/i18n`) is deliberately **not** reused: its
`discoverStringSources`/`keys.ts` merge everything into one `WebComponentStrings`-shaped bundle consumed by
`registerLocalized()`, which only makes sense for `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom elements. Generalizing
that shared, already-published package's public type surface just to fit CLI strings would be a bigger,
riskier change than building a small, self-contained i18n slice per CLI package on top of the shared
low-level adapter — matching this repo's existing convention of per-package codegen scripts (each of
`packages/scaffold`, `packages/scaffold-base`, and `packages/i18n` already has its own `scripts/generate.ts`
rather than a shared runner).

## Phase 0.5 — CLI string localization infrastructure

Each of `packages/scaffold` and `ai/pantoken-ai` gets its own small, self-contained i18n slice — no shared
runner, matching this repo's per-package-codegen convention (Phase 0's rationale). The two slices are
identical in shape; described once here for `packages/scaffold`, with `ai/pantoken-ai`'s copy noted in
Phase 4.

**New file `packages/scaffold/src/i18n.json`** — flat `{ key: englishValue }` map of every user-facing
string the CLI prints or shows in a prompt: platform-select prompt message and per-platform option labels,
directory-prompt message/placeholder, spinner text, `✓ wrote <path>` template, the "Next steps" block, and
every user-facing error message (`ScaffoldCliError` messages, the "Cancelled." message). Argument/option
**descriptions** shown in `--help` are included too, so `--help` itself localizes.

**New file `packages/scaffold/i18n-cache/en.json`** — committed cache, one entry per key, English value
copied verbatim (this is the identity/source-of-truth locale, always in sync with `src/i18n.json` by
construction).

**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/i18n-translate.ts`** — a human-run script (added to `package.json`
as `"i18n:translate": "node scripts/i18n-translate.ts"`, **not** part of the routine `generate`/`test`/
`check` scripts, matching `packages/i18n`'s `translate` vs. `generate` split): reads `src/i18n.json` and
each target locale's `i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, diffs for new/changed keys (content-addressed via `sha256`
from `@pantoken/translation-adapters`, same technique as `TranslationMemory`), and for each miss calls
`spawnPrompt()` (from `@pantoken/translation-adapters`) with a short "translate these UI strings from
English into `<locale>`" prompt — the same `claude -p` / `agy` CLI-spawn mechanism used by
`docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`'s `AiTranslationAdapter` and `packages/i18n`'s `translation-adapter.ts`,
selectable via a `SCAFFOLD_I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`/`_ARGS` env var pair for consistency with the existing
`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`/`I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND` precedent. Writes results back into
`i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, to be committed.

**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/generate.ts`** (extend the existing one) — add an offline,
network-free step that reads `src/i18n.json` + every committed `i18n-cache/*.json` and writes
`packages/scaffold/generated/locales/<locale>.ts` (each exporting a plain `Record<string, string>`), plus
`packages/scaffold/generated/locales/index.ts` (a small `{ en: ..., hu: ... }` map). Any key present in
`src/i18n.json` but missing from a non-English cache file is simply omitted from that locale's generated
object — the runtime lookup (below) falls back to English for it. This step runs as part of the existing
`vp run generate` (already invoked by `test`/`check`), so it never needs network access.

**New file `packages/scaffold/src/locale.ts`**:

```ts
export interface LocaleLookup {
  readonly locale: string;
  t(key: string): string;
}

/** Resolves the active locale: --lang flag > LC_ALL/LANG env > Intl > "en". */
export function detectLocale(options: {
  langFlag?: string;
  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  intl?: () => string; // injectable for tests; defaults to Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale
}): string;

/** Builds a lookup over the given locale bundles, falling back to `bundles[fallback]` (default "en")
 *  for any key missing in the resolved locale. Generic — reused as-is by ai/pantoken-ai for its own
 *  bundles (see Phase 4), not tied to scaffold's specific keys. */
export function createLocaleLookup(
  bundles: Record<string, Record<string, string>>,
  resolvedLocale: string,
  fallback?: string,
): LocaleLookup;
```

`createScaffoldCommand()` (Phase 1) adds a `--lang <tag>` option (e.g. `-l, --lang <tag>`) so a user can
override auto-detection explicitly; `resolveScaffoldTarget`/the action handler call
`detectLocale({ langFlag: opts.lang })` once, build the lookup via `createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, locale)`
(importing the generated `LOCALES` map from `generated/locales/index.ts`), and thread `t` through to every
place a string is printed or passed to a clack prompt's `message`/`placeholder`.

**Both `createLocaleLookup` and `detectLocale` are exported from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`** so
`ai/pantoken-ai` reuses them verbatim for its own separate bundle (Phase 4) instead of duplicating the
detection/fallback logic.

Translations are **not required to exist for this change to land safely**: `generate` succeeds with only
`en` populated, and `createLocaleLookup`'s fallback means the CLI is simply all-English until someone runs
`i18n:translate` for `hu` and commits the result — matching exactly how docs' Hungarian translations were
introduced (a manual, separate, later step, not a blocker on the code shipping).

1	# Rebuild pantoken's scaffold CLI on commander + @clack/prompts + @bomb.sh/tab
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	pantoken's scaffolding tools (`npx create-pantoken-app`, `npx @pantoken/scaffold`, `npx pantoken-ai
6	scaffold`) are three independently hand-rolled argv parsers with no real help system, no shell
7	completions, and thin/inconsistent interactivity. Each was built by hand with manual `argv.indexOf`/`for`
8	loops rather than a real CLI library, so none of them has auto-generated `--help`, none supports shell
9	completions, and each has its own slightly different error-message style and next-steps text. The goal is
10	to make `create-pantoken-app` (and its siblings) feel like a modern, complete scaffolding CLI — rich
11	interactive mode, a real silent/CI mode, full `--help`, and shell completions — while keeping
12	`npx create-pantoken-app <platform> [--dir]` working exactly as it does today for anyone already using it.
13	
14	Research (verified against npm/GitHub, not assumed) ruled out several alternatives: `clipanion` (no
15	commits since 2024), `oclif` (excellent completions story but architecturally overkill for a
16	single-command tool), `prompts` and `enquirer` (both stale, ~3 years without a release despite high
17	legacy download counts), and `crustjs` (Bun-only runtime — incompatible with the `npx`/Node contract this
18	CLI must support on any machine). The chosen stack — **commander** (arg parsing/help, the same choice
19	Svelte's `sv` CLI makes for an equivalent platform-picker scaffolder) + **`@clack/prompts`** (interactive
20	prompts, already a transitive dependency here via `bingo-stratum`/`@changesets/cli`, and the library both
21	`create-vite` and `create-vue` have migrated to) + **`@bomb.sh/tab`** (shell completions for bash/zsh/fish/
22	PowerShell, with a verified first-party commander adapter) — was chosen deliberately over these
23	alternatives and over rolling anything by hand again.
24	
25	This also consolidates `ai/pantoken-ai`'s separate hand-rolled `init`/`scaffold` CLI onto the same engine,
26	per this repo's own convention of updating `@pantoken/ai` alongside user-facing scaffold changes so
27	guidance doesn't drift — reducing three duplicate parsers to one shared foundation.
28	
29	This is a clean rewrite, not a backward-compatible refactor: the old argv contract, exact error-message
30	wording, and internal exports (`shouldPromptForDir`, etc.) are not preserved. Every affected package's
31	changeset is a `major` bump, calling out the behavior change plainly rather than papering over it with a
32	compat shim.
33	
34	The CLI's own prose (prompts, help text, error messages, next-steps output) is also localized: the CLI
35	detects the invoking terminal's language and shows translated strings where available, falling back to
36	English. This reuses `@pantoken/translation-adapters` — the generic, already-existing low-level piece
37	(`spawnPrompt`, `TranslationMemory`) that both the docs site and `@pantoken/i18n` build their own
38	translation pipelines on — rather than `@pantoken/i18n` itself, whose public runtime API
39	(`registerLocalized`, `LocaleBundle`) is tightly coupled to `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom-element
40	registration and isn't a generic message catalog. See Phase 0.5.
41	
42	Out of scope, explicitly: the Bingo presets being empty stubs (`blocks: []`, so real generation always
43	falls through to the legacy `SCAFFOLDS` string-template system) and the orphaned `next` platform template
44	— template-content issues, unrelated to this CLI-UX layer. `packages/cli` (`@pantoken/cli`, native-token
45	generation) is a different domain and is not touched.
46	
47	## Stack
48	
49	- **commander** `^15.0.0` + **`@commander-js/extra-typings`** `^15.0.0` (typed `.opts()`), new catalog
50	  entries in [pnpm-workspace.yaml](pnpm-workspace.yaml).
51	- **`@clack/prompts`** `^1.7.0` — promoted from transitive to a direct dependency of `@pantoken/scaffold`.
52	- **`@bomb.sh/tab`** `^0.0.22` — completions engine, verified commander adapter:
53	  `import tab from '@bomb.sh/tab/commander'; tab(program, { completionCommandName: 'completion' })`,
54	  generating `<cli> completion <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>`.
55	
56	Two other Bombshell-org packages were considered and rejected:
57	
58	- **`@bomb.sh/args`** (v0.3.1, published Feb 2025, ~11K downloads/week) — a real package, but a minimal
59	  (<1kB) flag-only parser: no subcommands, no auto-generated `--help`, no choices/enum validation, and
60	  notably **not** one of `@bomb.sh/tab`'s own supported adapters (tab only ships adapters for cac, citty,
61	  and commander — confirmed directly from its docs). Using it would mean giving up the exact
62	  subcommand/help/validation features this plan needs, and hand-writing an unproven custom tab adapter.
63	- **`@bomb.sh/tty`** (v0.8.0, created June 2026, ~93 downloads/week) — exists, but is a different category
64	  of tool entirely: a low-level, zero-I/O, WASM-compiled terminal *rendering engine* (flexbox-style layout
65	  via Clay), meant as a foundation for building full interactive TUI frameworks — not a prompts library.
66	  Massive overkill for a platform/directory prompt wizard; `@clack/prompts` already covers this need.
67	
68	For localization, **`@pantoken/translation-adapters`** (`tools/translation-adapters`, exports `TranslationMemory`,
69	`spawnPrompt`, `sha256`) is reused directly — it's the generic adapter-spawning/caching core, with no
70	markdown or web-components coupling. `@pantoken/i18n` (`packages/i18n`) is deliberately **not** reused: its
71	`discoverStringSources`/`keys.ts` merge everything into one `WebComponentStrings`-shaped bundle consumed by
72	`registerLocalized()`, which only makes sense for `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom elements. Generalizing
73	that shared, already-published package's public type surface just to fit CLI strings would be a bigger,
74	riskier change than building a small, self-contained i18n slice per CLI package on top of the shared
75	low-level adapter — matching this repo's existing convention of per-package codegen scripts (each of
76	`packages/scaffold`, `packages/scaffold-base`, and `packages/i18n` already has its own `scripts/generate.ts`
77	rather than a shared runner).
78	
79	## Branch and commit workflow
80	
81	Work happens on a new feature branch off `main` (e.g. `feat/scaffold-cli-commander-clack`), not directly
82	on `main`. Commit incrementally per phase using this repo's existing conventional-commit style (confirmed
83	from git history: `feat(scope): ...`, `fix(scope): ...`, `test(scope): ...`, `docs(scope): ...`,
84	`chore(scope): ...`), pushing the branch after each commit so progress is visible, then opening a pull
85	request once the full plan is implemented and verified:
86	
87	1. `chore(scaffold): add commander, @clack/prompts, @bomb.sh/tab, and @pantoken/translation-adapters to the
88	   catalog` — Phase 0.
89	2. `feat(scaffold): add CLI string localization infrastructure (en)` — Phase 0.5, English only; `hu` comes
90	   later once strings stabilize (commit 3 or a follow-up amendment to this one, implementer's judgment).
91	3. `feat(scaffold): rebuild the shared CLI on commander, @clack/prompts, and localized strings` — Phase 1 +
92	   the `packages/scaffold/tests/cli.test.ts` and `locale.test.ts` additions from Phase 5, plus running
93	   `i18n:translate` for `hu` and committing the result (keep implementation and its own tests in the same
94	   commit so `vp test` stays green at each step).
95	4. `feat(create-pantoken-app): pass --version and --lang through to the shared CLI` — Phase 2–3 (small;
96	   could also fold into commit 3 if trivial enough once written).
97	5. `feat(ai): consolidate the pantoken-ai CLI onto the shared commander engine, with its own localization`
98	   — Phase 4 (including its own i18n slice) + its new `ai/pantoken-ai/tests/cli.test.ts` from Phase 5.
99	6. `docs(scaffold): document --yes, --lang, completions, and package-manager detection` — Phase 6.
100	7. `chore: add changeset for the scaffold CLI rewrite` — Phase 7.
101	
102	Each commit should leave the repo in a green state (`vp test` / `vp check` passing for the touched
103	packages) rather than landing as one large commit at the end. Push after each commit lands. Do not open
104	the pull request until the full `pnpm run ready` gate (see Verification) passes.
105	
106	## Phase 0 — Catalog and dependency setup
107	
108	- [pnpm-workspace.yaml](pnpm-workspace.yaml): add `commander`, `@commander-js/extra-typings`,
109	  `@clack/prompts`, `@bomb.sh/tab` catalog entries, matching the existing style.
110	- [packages/scaffold/package.json](packages/scaffold/package.json): add all four as `dependencies`
111	  (`catalog:`).
112	- [ai/pantoken-ai/package.json](ai/pantoken-ai/package.json): add `commander`, `@commander-js/extra-typings`,
113	  `@bomb.sh/tab` as `dependencies` (catalog:). **Not** `@clack/prompts` — it only calls into
114	  `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`'s exported functions, which use clack internally; declaring it again would be
115	  redundant since `@pantoken/scaffold` already carries it as a real (non-dev) dependency.
116	- `packages/create-pantoken-app/package.json` — no changes; stays dependency-free beyond
117	  `@pantoken/scaffold: workspace:*`.
118	- [ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts): add an explicit
119	  `pack: { entry: { index: "src/index.ts", cli: "src/cli.ts" }, exports: true }`, mirroring
120	  [packages/scaffold/vite.config.ts](packages/scaffold/vite.config.ts) exactly, so the new `src/cli.ts`
121	  builds to `dist/cli.mjs`.
122	- `packages/scaffold/package.json` and `ai/pantoken-ai/package.json`: add
123	  `"@pantoken/translation-adapters": "workspace:*"` as a **devDependency** on both (build-script-only; never
124	  imported at runtime by the shipped CLI).
125	
126	## Phase 0.5 — CLI string localization infrastructure
127	
128	Each of `packages/scaffold` and `ai/pantoken-ai` gets its own small, self-contained i18n slice — no shared
129	runner, matching this repo's per-package-codegen convention (Phase 0's rationale). The two slices are
130	identical in shape; described once here for `packages/scaffold`, with `ai/pantoken-ai`'s copy noted in
131	Phase 4.
132	
133	**New file `packages/scaffold/src/i18n.json`** — flat `{ key: englishValue }` map of every user-facing
134	string the CLI prints or shows in a prompt: platform-select prompt message and per-platform option labels,
135	directory-prompt message/placeholder, spinner text, `✓ wrote <path>` template, the "Next steps" block, and
136	every user-facing error message (`ScaffoldCliError` messages, the "Cancelled." message). Argument/option
137	**descriptions** shown in `--help` are included too, so `--help` itself localizes.
138	
139	**New file `packages/scaffold/i18n-cache/en.json`** — committed cache, one entry per key, English value
140	copied verbatim (this is the identity/source-of-truth locale, always in sync with `src/i18n.json` by
141	construction).
142	
143	**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/i18n-translate.ts`** — a human-run script (added to `package.json`
144	as `"i18n:translate": "node scripts/i18n-translate.ts"`, **not** part of the routine `generate`/`test`/
145	`check` scripts, matching `packages/i18n`'s `translate` vs. `generate` split): reads `src/i18n.json` and
146	each target locale's `i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, diffs for new/changed keys (content-addressed via `sha256`
147	from `@pantoken/translation-adapters`, same technique as `TranslationMemory`), and for each miss calls
148	`spawnPrompt()` (from `@pantoken/translation-adapters`) with a short "translate these UI strings from
149	English into `<locale>`" prompt — the same `claude -p` / `agy` CLI-spawn mechanism used by
150	`docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`'s `AiTranslationAdapter` and `packages/i18n`'s `translation-adapter.ts`,
151	selectable via a `SCAFFOLD_I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`/`_ARGS` env var pair for consistency with the existing
152	`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`/`I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND` precedent. Writes results back into
153	`i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, to be committed.
154	
155	**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/generate.ts`** (extend the existing one) — add an offline,
156	network-free step that reads `src/i18n.json` + every committed `i18n-cache/*.json` and writes
157	`packages/scaffold/generated/locales/<locale>.ts` (each exporting a plain `Record<string, string>`), plus
158	`packages/scaffold/generated/locales/index.ts` (a small `{ en: ..., hu: ... }` map). Any key present in
159	`src/i18n.json` but missing from a non-English cache file is simply omitted from that locale's generated
160	object — the runtime lookup (below) falls back to English for it. This step runs as part of the existing
161	`vp run generate` (already invoked by `test`/`check`), so it never needs network access.
162	
163	**New file `packages/scaffold/src/locale.ts`**:
164	
165	```ts
166	export interface LocaleLookup {
167	  readonly locale: string;
168	  /** Looks up `key`, substituting any `{{param}}` placeholders from `params`. */
169	  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, string>): string;
170	}
171	
172	/** Resolves the active locale: --lang flag > LC_ALL/LANG env > Intl > "en". */
173	export function detectLocale(options: {
174	  langFlag?: string;
175	  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
176	  intl?: () => string; // injectable for tests; defaults to Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale
177	}): string;
178	
179	/** Builds a lookup over the given locale bundles, falling back to `bundles[fallback]` (default "en")
180	 *  for any key missing in the resolved locale. Generic — reused as-is by ai/pantoken-ai for its own
181	 *  bundles (see Phase 4), not tied to scaffold's specific keys. */
182	export function createLocaleLookup(
183	  bundles: Record<string, Record<string, string>>,
184	  resolvedLocale: string,
185	  fallback?: string,
186	): LocaleLookup;
187	```
188	
189	`createScaffoldCommand()` (Phase 1) adds a `--lang <tag>` option (e.g. `-l, --lang <tag>`) so a user can
190	override auto-detection explicitly; `resolveScaffoldTarget`/the action handler call
191	`detectLocale({ langFlag: opts.lang })` once, build the lookup via `createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, locale)`
192	(importing the generated `LOCALES` map from `generated/locales/index.ts`), and thread `t` through to every
193	place a string is printed or passed to a clack prompt's `message`/`placeholder`.
194	
195	**Both `createLocaleLookup` and `detectLocale` are exported from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`** so
196	`ai/pantoken-ai` reuses them verbatim for its own separate bundle (Phase 4) instead of duplicating the
197	detection/fallback logic.
198	
199	Translations are **not required to exist for this change to land safely**: `generate` succeeds with only
200	`en` populated, and `createLocaleLookup`'s fallback means the CLI is simply all-English until someone runs
201	`i18n:translate` for `hu` and commits the result — matching exactly how docs' Hungarian translations were
202	introduced (a manual, separate, later step, not a blocker on the code shipping).
203	
204	## Phase 1 — Rewrite `packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts`
205	
206	Replace the manual `parseArgs` loop and raw `readline` prompt with a commander-based builder, exporting
207	granular, independently reusable pieces (not one opaque function) so `ai/pantoken-ai` can compose its own
208	subcommand from the same logic instead of reimplementing it a third time.
209	
210	New exports from [packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts](packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts):
211	
212	```ts
213	export { SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS, isScaffoldPlatform } from "./index.ts";
214	export { detectLocale, createLocaleLookup, type LocaleLookup } from "./locale.ts";
215	export { LOCALES } from "../generated/locales/index.ts";
216	
217	/** Thrown for user-facing CLI errors (e.g. missing platform under --yes); carries an exit code. */
218	export class ScaffoldCliError extends Error {
219	  constructor(message: string, public readonly exitCode = 1) { super(message); }
220	}
221	
222	/** Whether a value should be interactively prompted for: no value given, not --yes, and stdin is a TTY. */
223	export function shouldPrompt(value: string | undefined, opts: { yes?: boolean; isTTY?: boolean }): boolean;
224	
225	export interface ResolveScaffoldTargetOptions {
226	  platformArg?: string;
227	  dirOption?: string;
228	  yes?: boolean;
229	  isTTY?: boolean; // injectable for tests; defaults to process.stdin.isTTY
230	  t: LocaleLookup["t"];
231	}
232	
233	/** Resolves platform + directory: prompts via clack select()/text() when omitted on a TTY (not --yes);
234	 *  throws ScaffoldCliError with a clear, localized message when a required value is missing
235	 *  non-interactively. All prompt copy (message/placeholder/option labels) is looked up via `t`. */
236	export async function resolveScaffoldTarget(
237	  options: ResolveScaffoldTargetOptions,
238	): Promise<{ platform: ScaffoldPlatform; dir: string }>;
239	
240	/** Runs scaffoldProject() wrapped in a clack spinner() whose start/stop text comes from `t`; returns the
241	 *  written paths. */
242	export async function scaffoldWithSpinner(
243	  platform: ScaffoldPlatform,
244	  dir: string,
245	  t: LocaleLookup["t"],
246	): Promise<string[]>;
247	
248	/** Detects the invoking package manager from npm_config_user_agent (the create-vite/create-vue technique). */
249	export function detectPackageManager(env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): "npm" | "pnpm" | "yarn" | "bun" | undefined;
250	
251	/** Prints the post-scaffold "Next steps" block, leading with the detected package manager's install
252	 *  command (falling back to a generic localized "install dependencies" line when detection fails). All
253	 *  copy comes from `t`. */
254	export function printNextSteps(dir: string, written: string[], t: LocaleLookup["t"]): void;
255	
256	/** Shared commander Argument validator for the platform positional (used by all three CLIs so the
257	 *  error wording has one source of truth). Throws commander.InvalidArgumentError. */
258	export function validateScaffoldPlatform(value: string): string;
259	
260	export interface ScaffoldCommandOptions {
261	  name?: string;           // program name shown in help/usage; default "pantoken-scaffold"
262	  usageCommand?: string;   // exact invocation string for help examples; defaults to `name`
263	  version?: string;        // no default — callers pass their own package.json version
264	  enableCompletions?: boolean; // default true
265	}
266	
267	/** Builds the full, ready-to-parse commander Command for pantoken-scaffold/create-pantoken-app. */
268	export function createScaffoldCommand(options?: ScaffoldCommandOptions): Command;
269	
270	/** Entry point both bin shims call: builds the command and parses argv against it. */
271	export async function runScaffoldCli(
272	  argv: string[],
273	  options: { usageCommand: string; version?: string },
274	): Promise<void>;
275	```

277	`shouldPromptForDir` is removed, generalized into `shouldPrompt` (now covers both platform and dir) — one
278	of several deliberate breaking changes to this module's previously-exported, `@alpha`-tagged surface (no
279	backward compatibility is being preserved here; see the changeset in Phase 7).

281	### `createScaffoldCommand()` shape

283	```ts
284	import { InvalidArgumentError } from "commander";
285	import { Argument, Command } from "@commander-js/extra-typings";
286	import tab from "@bomb.sh/tab/commander";

288	const program = new Command(options?.name ?? "pantoken-scaffold")
289	  .exitOverride() // throw CommanderError instead of calling process.exit — makes parseAsync() safe
290	  .configureOutput({
291	    writeOut: (s) => process.stdout.write(s),
292	    writeErr: (s) => process.stderr.write(s),
293	  })
294	  .addArgument(
295	    new Argument(

297	      `Platform to scaffold (${SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join("|")}; "html" is an alias for "components")`,
298	    ).argParser(validateScaffoldPlatform),
299	  )

301	  .option("-y, --yes", "Never prompt; error instead of prompting for a missing platform/directory", false)
302	  .option("-l, --lang <tag>", "Override the auto-detected display language (e.g. \"hu\")");
303	
304	if (options?.version) program.version(options.version, "-v, --version");
305	
306	program.action(async (platformArg, opts) => {
307	  const locale = detectLocale({ langFlag: opts.lang });
308	  const { t } = createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, locale);
309	  const { platform, dir } = await resolveScaffoldTarget({ platformArg, dirOption: opts.dir, yes: opts.yes, t });
310	  const written = await scaffoldWithSpinner(platform, dir, t);

319	Key precision points:
320	
321	- **Platform validation happens via `Argument.argParser`, not `.choices()`** — `.choices()` can't be used
322	  because `"html"` must validate (it's an alias in `isScaffoldPlatform`, not a member of
323	  `SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS`). The error becomes commander's own
324	  `error: command-argument value '...' is invalid for argument 'platform'. <message>` format — a
325	  user-visible wording change from today's `Unknown platform "...".`, intentional and covered in Phase 5.
326	- **A second stray positional** (e.g. `pantoken-scaffold react extra`) is now rejected by commander itself
327	  ("too many arguments") since only one `[platform]` argument is declared — replaces today's
328	  `Unknown option "extra".` with commander's own wording. Deliberate, acceptable change.
329	- **`.exitOverride()` + `.configureOutput()`** is the standard commander pattern for using a `Command` from
330	  library code and for unit-testing without a real `process.exit` — it throws `CommanderError` (carrying
331	  `.exitCode` and `.code`, e.g. `"commander.helpDisplayed"`, `"commander.version"`,
332	  `"commander.invalidArgument"`) instead of exiting or bypassing mocked I/O.
333	- **`--yes`/`-y`** forces `resolveScaffoldTarget` to skip both prompts; if platform is still missing, it
334	  throws `ScaffoldCliError('Missing required argument "platform". Expected one of: ...')`. `--yes` does not
335	  require `--dir` — directory still silently defaults to `"."` when omitted, matching today's non-TTY
336	  default.

338	### `resolveScaffoldTarget` internals
339	
340	- Platform: `resolveScaffoldTarget` validates `platformArg` itself (via `isScaffoldPlatform`) even though
341	  `createScaffoldCommand`'s own argParser already validated it — this makes it safe to call from
342	  `ai/pantoken-ai`'s subcommand too, which attaches the same validator independently (see Phase 4).
343	- If `platformArg` is omitted: `shouldPrompt(platformArg, { yes, isTTY })` false → throw
344	  `ScaffoldCliError` (missing platform, non-interactive; message from
345	  `t("errorMissingPlatform", { platforms: SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join(", ") })`). True →
346	  `select({ message: t("promptPlatform"), options: SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.map(p => ({ value: p, label: p })) })`
347	  (the platform values themselves — `"react"`, `"vue"`, etc. — are identifiers, not translated); on
348	  `isCancel(result)` → `cancel(t("cancelled"))`, throw `ScaffoldCliError(t("cancelled"), 1)`.
349	- Directory: same `shouldPrompt` gate; `text({ message: t("promptDir"), placeholder: ".", defaultValue: "." })`
350	  (clack returns the default on empty Enter, replacing the old manual `.trim() || "."`). Same cancel
351	  handling.

353	### `printNextSteps` — package-manager detection, wired in

355	`detectPackageManager()` parses `process.env.npm_config_user_agent` (the same technique `create-vite`/
356	`create-vue` use) to get `"npm" | "pnpm" | "yarn" | "bun"`. `printNextSteps` prints a localized
357	`t("nextStepsInstall", { command: "<detected> install" })` line, falling back to a generic localized
358	"install dependencies" line when detection fails. This is a real, intentional output change from today's
359	static English text — three existing test assertions that check for the literal `"vp install"` string need

384	  }
