input.plan:
# Rebuild pantoken's scaffold CLI on commander + @clack/prompts + @bomb.sh/tab

## Context

pantoken's scaffolding tools (`npx create-pantoken-app`, `npx @pantoken/scaffold`, `npx pantoken-ai
scaffold`) are three independently hand-rolled argv parsers with no real help system, no shell
completions, and thin/inconsistent interactivity. Each was built by hand with manual `argv.indexOf`/`for`
loops rather than a real CLI library, so none of them has auto-generated `--help`, none supports shell
completions, and each has its own slightly different error-message style and next-steps text. The goal is
to make `create-pantoken-app` (and its siblings) feel like a modern, complete scaffolding CLI — rich
interactive mode, a real silent/CI mode, full `--help`, and shell completions — while keeping
`npx create-pantoken-app <platform> [--dir]` working exactly as it does today for anyone already using it.

Research (verified against npm/GitHub, not assumed) ruled out several alternatives: `clipanion` (no
commits since 2024), `oclif` (excellent completions story but architecturally overkill for a
single-command tool), `prompts` and `enquirer` (both stale, ~3 years without a release despite high
legacy download counts), and `crustjs` (Bun-only runtime — incompatible with the `npx`/Node contract this
CLI must support on any machine). The chosen stack — **commander** (arg parsing/help, the same choice
Svelte's `sv` CLI makes for an equivalent platform-picker scaffolder) + **`@clack/prompts`** (interactive
prompts, already a transitive dependency here via `bingo-stratum`/`@changesets/cli`, and the library both
`create-vite` and `create-vue` have migrated to) + **`@bomb.sh/tab`** (shell completions for bash/zsh/fish/
PowerShell, with a verified first-party commander adapter) — was chosen deliberately over these
alternatives and over rolling anything by hand again.

This also consolidates `ai/pantoken-ai`'s separate hand-rolled `init`/`scaffold` CLI onto the same engine,
per this repo's own convention of updating `@pantoken/ai` alongside user-facing scaffold changes so
guidance doesn't drift — reducing three duplicate parsers to one shared foundation.

This is a clean rewrite, not a backward-compatible refactor: the old argv contract, exact error-message
wording, and internal exports (`shouldPromptForDir`, etc.) are not preserved. Every affected package's
changeset is a `major` bump, calling out the behavior change plainly rather than papering over it with a
compat shim.

The CLI's own prose (prompts, help text, error messages, next-steps output) is also localized: the CLI
detects the invoking terminal's language and shows translated strings where available, falling back to
English. This reuses `@pantoken/translation-adapters` — the generic, already-existing low-level piece
(`spawnPrompt`, `TranslationMemory`) that both the docs site and `@pantoken/i18n` build their own
translation pipelines on — rather than `@pantoken/i18n` itself, whose public runtime API
(`registerLocalized`, `LocaleBundle`) is tightly coupled to `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom-element
registration and isn't a generic message catalog. See Phase 0.5.

Out of scope, explicitly: the Bingo presets being empty stubs (`blocks: []`, so real generation always
falls through to the legacy `SCAFFOLDS` string-template system) and the orphaned `next` platform template
— template-content issues, unrelated to this CLI-UX layer. `packages/cli` (`@pantoken/cli`, native-token
generation) is a different domain and is not touched.

## Stack

- **commander** `^15.0.0` + **`@commander-js/extra-typings`** `^15.0.0` (typed `.opts()`), new catalog
  entries in [pnpm-workspace.yaml](pnpm-workspace.yaml).
- **`@clack/prompts`** `^1.7.0` — promoted from transitive to a direct dependency of `@pantoken/scaffold`.
- **`@bomb.sh/tab`** `^0.0.22` — completions engine, verified commander adapter:
  `import tab from '@bomb.sh/tab/commander'; tab(program, { completionCommandName: 'completion' })`,
  generating `<cli> completion <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>`.

Two other Bombshell-org packages were considered and rejected:

- **`@bomb.sh/args`** (v0.3.1, published Feb 2025, ~11K downloads/week) — a real package, but a minimal
  (<1kB) flag-only parser: no subcommands, no auto-generated `--help`, no choices/enum validation, and
  notably **not** one of `@bomb.sh/tab`'s own supported adapters (tab only ships adapters for cac, citty,
  and commander — confirmed directly from its docs). Using it would mean giving up the exact
  subcommand/help/validation features this plan needs, and hand-writing an unproven custom tab adapter.
- **`@bomb.sh/tty`** (v0.8.0, created June 2026, ~93 downloads/week) — exists, but is a different category
  of tool entirely: a low-level, zero-I/O, WASM-compiled terminal *rendering engine* (flexbox-style layout
  via Clay), meant as a foundation for building full interactive TUI frameworks — not a prompts library.
  Massive overkill for a platform/directory prompt wizard; `@clack/prompts` already covers this need.

For localization, **`@pantoken/translation-adapters`** (`tools/translation-adapters`, exports `TranslationMemory`,
`spawnPrompt`, `sha256`) is reused directly — it's the generic adapter-spawning/caching core, with no
markdown or web-components coupling. `@pantoken/i18n` (`packages/i18n`) is deliberately **not** reused: its
`discoverStringSources`/`keys.ts` merge everything into one `WebComponentStrings`-shaped bundle consumed by
`registerLocalized()`, which only makes sense for `@pantoken/web-components`'s custom elements. Generalizing
that shared, already-published package's public type surface just to fit CLI strings would be a bigger,
riskier change than building a small, self-contained i18n slice per CLI package on top of the shared
low-level adapter — matching this repo's existing convention of per-package codegen scripts (each of
`packages/scaffold`, `packages/scaffold-base`, and `packages/i18n` already has its own `scripts/generate.ts`
rather than a shared runner).

## Branch and commit workflow

Work happens on a new feature branch off `main` (e.g. `feat/scaffold-cli-commander-clack`), not directly
on `main`. Commit incrementally per phase using this repo's existing conventional-commit style (confirmed
from git history: `feat(scope): ...`, `fix(scope): ...`, `test(scope): ...`, `docs(scope): ...`,
`chore(scope): ...`), pushing the branch after each commit so progress is visible, then opening a pull
request once the full plan is implemented and verified:

1. `chore(scaffold): add commander, @clack/prompts, @bomb.sh/tab, and @pantoken/translation-adapters to the
   catalog` — Phase 0.
2. `feat(scaffold): add CLI string localization infrastructure (en)` — Phase 0.5, English only; `hu` comes
   later once strings stabilize (commit 4 or a follow-up amendment to this one, implementer's judgment).
3. `feat: restructure translation tasks (ui:*/docs:translate/cli:*) and fold CLI drift into i18n:check:drift`
   — Phase 0.6: the `vite.config.ts` task renames/additions, the widened `.vite-hooks/pre-push` pattern, and
   the `ci.yml` path-filter + `ci-gate` changes. Lands after Phase 0.5 so `@pantoken/scaffold#translate`/
   `#check:drift` already exist for the new `cli:translate`/`i18n:check:drift` commands to reference; lands
   before `ai/pantoken-ai`'s own slice (commit 6) is required, since `vp run @pantoken/ai#translate` simply
   won't exist to fail on until then — sequence this commit after Phase 4 instead if that ordering is
   easier in practice (implementer's judgment; either order is safe as long as both packages' scripts exist
   before the combined `cli:translate`/`i18n:check:drift` commands are exercised in CI).
4. `feat(scaffold): rebuild the shared CLI on commander, @clack/prompts, and localized strings` — Phase 1 +
   the `packages/scaffold/tests/cli.test.ts` and `locale.test.ts` additions from Phase 5, plus running
   `vp run @pantoken/scaffold#translate` for `hu` and committing the result (keep implementation and its
   own tests in the same commit so `vp test` stays green at each step).
5. `feat(create-pantoken-app): pass --version and --lang through to the shared CLI` — Phase 2–3 (small;
   could also fold into commit 4 if trivial enough once written).
6. `feat(ai): consolidate the pantoken-ai CLI onto the shared commander engine, with its own localization`
   — Phase 4 (including its own i18n slice) + its new `ai/pantoken-ai/tests/cli.test.ts` from Phase 5.
7. `docs(scaffold): document --yes, --lang, completions, and package-manager detection` — Phase 6.
8. `chore: add changeset for the scaffold CLI rewrite` — Phase 7.

Each commit should leave the repo in a green state (`vp test` / `vp check` passing for the touched
packages) rather than landing as one large commit at the end. Push after each commit lands. Do not open
the pull request until the full `pnpm run ready` gate (see Verification) passes.

## Phase 0 — Catalog and dependency setup

- [pnpm-workspace.yaml](pnpm-workspace.yaml): add `commander`, `@commander-js/extra-typings`,
  `@clack/prompts`, `@bomb.sh/tab` catalog entries, matching the existing style.
- [packages/scaffold/package.json](packages/scaffold/package.json): add all four as `dependencies`
  (`catalog:`).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/package.json](ai/pantoken-ai/package.json): add `commander`, `@commander-js/extra-typings`,
  `@bomb.sh/tab` as `dependencies` (catalog:). **Not** `@clack/prompts` — it only calls into
  `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`'s exported functions, which use clack internally; declaring it again would be
  redundant since `@pantoken/scaffold` already carries it as a real (non-dev) dependency.
- `packages/create-pantoken-app/package.json` — no changes; stays dependency-free beyond
  `@pantoken/scaffold: workspace:*`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/vite.config.ts): add an explicit
  `pack: { entry: { index: "src/index.ts", cli: "src/cli.ts" }, exports: true }`, mirroring
  [packages/scaffold/vite.config.ts](packages/scaffold/vite.config.ts) exactly, so the new `src/cli.ts`
  builds to `dist/cli.mjs`.
- `packages/scaffold/package.json` and `ai/pantoken-ai/package.json`: add
  `"@pantoken/translation-adapters": "workspace:*"` as a **devDependency** on both (build-script-only; never
  imported at runtime by the shipped CLI).

## Phase 0.5 — CLI string localization infrastructure

Each of `packages/scaffold` and `ai/pantoken-ai` gets its own small, self-contained i18n slice — no shared
runner, matching this repo's per-package-codegen convention (Phase 0's rationale). The two slices are
identical in shape; described once here for `packages/scaffold`, with `ai/pantoken-ai`'s copy noted in
Phase 4.

**New file `packages/scaffold/src/i18n.json`** — flat `{ key: englishValue }` map of every user-facing
string the CLI prints or shows in a prompt: platform-select prompt message and per-platform option labels,
directory-prompt message/placeholder, spinner text, `✓ wrote <path>` template, the "Next steps" block, and
every user-facing error message (`ScaffoldCliError` messages, the "Cancelled." message). Argument/option
**descriptions** shown in `--help` are included too, so `--help` itself localizes.

**New file `packages/scaffold/i18n-cache/en.json`** — committed cache, one entry per key, English value
copied verbatim (this is the identity/source-of-truth locale, always in sync with `src/i18n.json` by
construction).

**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/translate.ts`** — a human-run script, **not** part of the routine
`generate`/`test`/`check` scripts (matching `packages/i18n`'s `translate` vs. `generate` split exactly):
reads `src/i18n.json` and each target locale's `i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, diffs for new/changed keys
(content-addressed via `sha256` from `@pantoken/translation-adapters`, same technique as
`TranslationMemory`), and for each miss calls `spawnPrompt()` (from `@pantoken/translation-adapters`) with
a short "translate these UI strings from English into `<locale>`" prompt. Writes results back into
`i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, to be committed. Two `package.json` scripts, named and shaped exactly like
`packages/i18n`'s own (reusing the same `I18N_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER`/`I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND` env vars —
no new package-specific env var names invented):

```json
"translate": "I18N_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=ai node scripts/translate.ts",
"translate:agy": "I18N_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=ai I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND=\"$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tools/translation-adapters/agy-wrapper.sh\" node scripts/translate.ts"
```

**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/check-drift.ts`** — mirrors `packages/i18n/scripts/check-bundle-drift.ts`:
fails (non-zero exit) if any key in `src/i18n.json` has no corresponding entry in a target locale's
committed `i18n-cache/<locale>.json`, so a contributor who adds/edits a CLI string without running
`translate` gets caught before merge, not silently shipped as an English fallback forever. Exposed as
`"check:drift": "node scripts/check-drift.ts"`, and folded into the package's own `"check"` script
(`"check": "vp run scan && vp check && node scripts/check-drift.ts"`) so `vp run check` catches it locally
too, in addition to the hook/CI wiring in Phase 0.6.

**New file `packages/scaffold/scripts/generate.ts`** (extend the existing one) — add an offline,
network-free step that reads `src/i18n.json` + every committed `i18n-cache/*.json` and writes
`packages/scaffold/generated/locales/<locale>.ts` (each exporting a plain `Record<string, string>`), plus
`packages/scaffold/generated/locales/index.ts` (a small `{ en: ..., hu: ... }` map). Any key present in
`src/i18n.json` but missing from a non-English cache file is simply omitted from that locale's generated
object — the runtime lookup (below) falls back to English for it. This step runs as part of the existing
`vp run generate` (already invoked by `test`/`check`), so it never needs network access.

**New file `packages/scaffold/src/locale.ts`**:

```ts
export interface LocaleLookup {
  readonly locale: string;
  /** Looks up `key`, substituting any `{{param}}` placeholders from `params`. */
  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, string>): string;
}

/** Resolves the active locale: --lang flag > LC_ALL/LANG env > Intl > "en". */
export function detectLocale(options: {
  langFlag?: string;
  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  intl?: () => string; // injectable for tests; defaults to Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale
}): string;

/** Builds a lookup over the given locale bundles, falling back to `bundles[fallback]` (default "en")
 *  for any key missing in the resolved locale. Generic — reused as-is by ai/pantoken-ai for its own
 *  bundles (see Phase 4), not tied to scaffold's specific keys. */
export function createLocaleLookup(
  bundles: Record<string, Record<string, string>>,
  resolvedLocale: string,
  fallback?: string,
): LocaleLookup;
```

`createScaffoldCommand()` (Phase 1) adds a `--lang <tag>` option (e.g. `-l, --lang <tag>`) so a user can
override auto-detection explicitly; `resolveScaffoldTarget`/the action handler call
`detectLocale({ langFlag: opts.lang })` once, build the lookup via `createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, locale)`
(importing the generated `LOCALES` map from `generated/locales/index.ts`), and thread `t` through to every
place a string is printed or passed to a clack prompt's `message`/`placeholder`.

**Both `createLocaleLookup` and `detectLocale` are exported from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`** so
`ai/pantoken-ai` reuses them verbatim for its own separate bundle (Phase 4) instead of duplicating the
detection/fallback logic.

Translations are **not required to exist for this change to land safely**: `generate` succeeds with only
`en` populated, and `createLocaleLookup`'s fallback means the CLI is simply all-English until someone runs
`i18n:translate` for `hu` and commits the result — matching exactly how docs' Hungarian translations were
introduced (a manual, separate, later step, not a blocker on the code shipping).

## Phase 0.6 — Translation task graph, drift checks, and hooks

This repo's translation tooling currently has three separate domains, each wired up slightly
inconsistently (verified directly from root `vite.config.ts`'s `run.tasks` block, `docs/package.json`,
`packages/i18n/package.json`, `.vite-hooks/pre-push`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — not assumed):

- **`packages/i18n`** (web-components UI strings) — root vp tasks `i18n:translate`/`i18n:translate:agy`
  (→ `vp run @pantoken/i18n#translate`/`translate:agy`), `i18n:check:drift`
  (→ `vp run @pantoken/i18n#check:drift`).
- **`docs`** (guides + API reference) — package-local npm scripts only: `docs:locales:translate`/
  `docs:locales:translate:agy`, `docs:check:drift`. A root vp task exists for the agy variant
  (`docs:translate:agy`) but **not** the claude variant — a pre-existing asymmetry.
- **CLI packages** (new, this plan) — nothing yet.

Restructure into one consistent naming scheme, and fold the two new CLI packages' drift checks into the
existing, already-hook-and-CI-gated `i18n:check:drift` umbrella (rather than leaving them as a fourth,
unwired check like `docs:check:drift` currently is).

**Root [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts) `run.tasks` changes:**

1. Rename the existing web-components-specific tasks so the `i18n:` prefix is free for the new umbrella
   meaning: `i18n:translate` → `ui:translate`, `i18n:translate:agy` → `ui:translate:agy` (commands
   unchanged: `vp run @pantoken/i18n#translate` / `#translate:agy`).
2. Add the missing `docs:translate` task (claude variant), matching the existing `docs:translate:agy`
   entry: `{ command: "vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:locales:translate", cache: false }`.
3. Add new CLI tasks, orchestrating both `packages/scaffold` and `ai/pantoken-ai` together (each package's
   own `translate`/`translate:agy` script, per Phase 0.5/4):
   ```ts
   "cli:translate:claude": {
     command: "vp run @pantoken/scaffold#translate && vp run @pantoken/ai#translate",
     cache: false,
   },
   "cli:translate:agy": {
     command: "vp run @pantoken/scaffold#translate:agy && vp run @pantoken/ai#translate:agy",
     cache: false,
   },
   "cli:translate": { command: "true", dependsOn: ["cli:translate:claude"] },
   ```
   (`cli:translate`'s bare name defaults to the claude-model variant, matching the existing
   bare-name-means-claude convention from `docs:api:locales`/`docs:guides:locales`.)
4. Re-implement `i18n:translate` as the one-shot top-level orchestrator the plan asks for, plus a matching
   `:agy` variant for symmetry:
   ```ts
   "i18n:translate": { command: "true", dependsOn: ["ui:translate", "docs:translate", "cli:translate"] },
   "i18n:translate:agy": {
     command: "true",
     dependsOn: ["ui:translate:agy", "docs:translate:agy", "cli:translate:agy"],
   },
   ```
   `vp run i18n:translate` now translates web-components strings, docs, and both CLIs' strings in one shot.
5. Extend `i18n:check:drift`'s command to also run the two new packages' drift checks:
   ```ts
   "i18n:check:drift": {
     command: "vp run @pantoken/i18n#check:drift && vp run @pantoken/scaffold#check:drift && vp run @pantoken/ai#check:drift",
   },
   ```
   The task name stays `i18n:check:drift` deliberately — everything that already depends on it (the
   pre-push hook, the CI job) picks up the new CLI checks automatically once its command is extended and
   the path filters below are widened; no hook/CI file needs to know these are "new" checks.

**[.vite-hooks/pre-push](.vite-hooks/pre-push) change** — widen the existing conditional's file-path
pattern so a push touching only the CLI packages' i18n files still triggers the (now-extended)
`i18n:check:drift`:

```diff
-if git diff --name-only "@{upstream}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^(packages/i18n/|renderers/web-components/src/lib/strings\.ts)'; then
+if git diff --name-only "@{upstream}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^(packages/i18n/|renderers/web-components/src/lib/strings\.ts|packages/scaffold/(src/i18n\.json|i18n-cache/)|ai/pantoken-ai/(src/i18n\.json|i18n-cache/))'; then
   vp run i18n:check:drift
 fi
```

**[.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) changes:**

1. Widen the `i18n-changes` job's `dorny/paths-filter` `i18n:` list to also match the two new packages'
   i18n files:
   ```diff
    i18n:
      - 'packages/i18n/**'
      - 'renderers/web-components/src/lib/strings.ts'
   +  - 'packages/scaffold/src/i18n.json'
   +  - 'packages/scaffold/i18n-cache/**'

export { SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS, isScaffoldPlatform } from "./index.ts";
export { detectLocale, createLocaleLookup, type LocaleLookup } from "./locale.ts";
export { LOCALES } from "../generated/locales/index.ts";

/** Thrown for user-facing CLI errors (e.g. missing platform under --yes); carries an exit code. */
export class ScaffoldCliError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, public readonly exitCode = 1) { super(message); }
}

/** Whether a value should be interactively prompted for: no value given, not --yes, and stdin is a TTY. */
export function shouldPrompt(value: string | undefined, opts: { yes?: boolean; isTTY?: boolean }): boolean;

export interface ResolveScaffoldTargetOptions {
  platformArg?: string;
  dirOption?: string;
  yes?: boolean;
  isTTY?: boolean; // injectable for tests; defaults to process.stdin.isTTY
  t: LocaleLookup["t"];
}

/** Resolves platform + directory: prompts via clack select()/text() when omitted on a TTY (not --yes);
 *  throws ScaffoldCliError with a clear, localized message when a required value is missing
 *  non-interactively. All prompt copy (message/placeholder/option labels) is looked up via `t`. */
export async function resolveScaffoldTarget(
  options: ResolveScaffoldTargetOptions,
): Promise<{ platform: ScaffoldPlatform; dir: string }>;

/** Runs scaffoldProject() wrapped in a clack spinner() whose start/stop text comes from `t`; returns the
 *  written paths. */
export async function scaffoldWithSpinner(
  platform: ScaffoldPlatform,
  dir: string,
  t: LocaleLookup["t"],
): Promise<string[]>;

/** Detects the invoking package manager from npm_config_user_agent (the create-vite/create-vue technique). */
export function detectPackageManager(env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): "npm" | "pnpm" | "yarn" | "bun" | undefined;

/** Prints the post-scaffold "Next steps" block, leading with the detected package manager's install
 *  command (falling back to a generic localized "install dependencies" line when detection fails). All
 *  copy comes from `t`. */
export function printNextSteps(dir: string, written: string[], t: LocaleLookup["t"]): void;

/** Shared commander Argument validator for the platform positional (used by all three CLIs so the
 *  error wording has one source of truth). Throws commander.InvalidArgumentError. */
export function validateScaffoldPlatform(value: string): string;

export interface ScaffoldCommandOptions {
  name?: string;           // program name shown in help/usage; default "pantoken-scaffold"
  usageCommand?: string;   // exact invocation string for help examples; defaults to `name`
  version?: string;        // no default — callers pass their own package.json version
  enableCompletions?: boolean; // default true
}

/** Builds the full, ready-to-parse commander Command for pantoken-scaffold/create-pantoken-app. */
export function createScaffoldCommand(options?: ScaffoldCommandOptions): Command;

/** Entry point both bin shims call: builds the command and parses argv against it. */
export async function runScaffoldCli(
  argv: string[],
  options: { usageCommand: string; version?: string },
): Promise<void>;

`shouldPromptForDir` is removed, generalized into `shouldPrompt` (now covers both platform and dir) — one
of several deliberate breaking changes to this module's previously-exported, `@alpha`-tagged surface (no
backward compatibility is being preserved here; see the changeset in Phase 7).

### `createScaffoldCommand()` shape

```ts
import { InvalidArgumentError } from "commander";
import { Argument, Command } from "@commander-js/extra-typings";
import tab from "@bomb.sh/tab/commander";

const program = new Command(options?.name ?? "pantoken-scaffold")
  .exitOverride() // throw CommanderError instead of calling process.exit — makes parseAsync() safe
  .configureOutput({
    writeOut: (s) => process.stdout.write(s),
    writeErr: (s) => process.stderr.write(s),
  })
  .addArgument(
    new Argument(
      "[platform]",
      `Platform to scaffold (${SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join("|")}; "html" is an alias for "components")`,
    ).argParser(validateScaffoldPlatform),
  )
  .option("-d, --dir <path>", "Target directory (prompts interactively on a TTY if omitted)")
  .option("-y, --yes", "Never prompt; error instead of prompting for a missing platform/directory", false)
  .option("-l, --lang <tag>", "Override the auto-detected display language (e.g. \"hu\")");

if (options?.version) program.version(options.version, "-v, --version");

program.action(async (platformArg, opts) => {
  const locale = detectLocale({ langFlag: opts.lang });
  const { t } = createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, locale);
  const { platform, dir } = await resolveScaffoldTarget({ platformArg, dirOption: opts.dir, yes: opts.yes, t });
  const written = await scaffoldWithSpinner(platform, dir, t);
  for (const path of written) console.log(t("wroteFile", { path }));
  printNextSteps(dir, written, t);
});

if (options?.enableCompletions ?? true) tab(program, { completionCommandName: "completion" });
return program;
```

Key precision points:

- **Platform validation happens via `Argument.argParser`, not `.choices()`** — `.choices()` can't be used
  because `"html"` must validate (it's an alias in `isScaffoldPlatform`, not a member of
  `SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS`). The error becomes commander's own
  `error: command-argument value '...' is invalid for argument 'platform'. <message>` format — a
  user-visible wording change from today's `Unknown platform "...".`, intentional and covered in Phase 5.
- **A second stray positional** (e.g. `pantoken-scaffold react extra`) is now rejected by commander itself
  ("too many arguments") since only one `[platform]` argument is declared — replaces today's
  `Unknown option "extra".` with commander's own wording. Deliberate, acceptable change.
- **`.exitOverride()` + `.configureOutput()`** is the standard commander pattern for using a `Command` from
  library code and for unit-testing without a real `process.exit` — it throws `CommanderError` (carrying
  `.exitCode` and `.code`, e.g. `"commander.helpDisplayed"`, `"commander.version"`,
  `"commander.invalidArgument"`) instead of exiting or bypassing mocked I/O.
- **`--yes`/`-y`** forces `resolveScaffoldTarget` to skip both prompts; if platform is still missing, it
  throws `ScaffoldCliError('Missing required argument "platform". Expected one of: ...')`. `--yes` does not
  require `--dir` — directory still silently defaults to `"."` when omitted, matching today's non-TTY
  default.

### `resolveScaffoldTarget` internals

- Platform: `resolveScaffoldTarget` validates `platformArg` itself (via `isScaffoldPlatform`) even though
  `createScaffoldCommand`'s own argParser already validated it — this makes it safe to call from
  `ai/pantoken-ai`'s subcommand too, which attaches the same validator independently (see Phase 4).
- If `platformArg` is omitted: `shouldPrompt(platformArg, { yes, isTTY })` false → throw
  `ScaffoldCliError` (missing platform, non-interactive; message from
  `t("errorMissingPlatform", { platforms: SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join(", ") })`). True →
  `select({ message: t("promptPlatform"), options: SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.map(p => ({ value: p, label: p })) })`
  (the platform values themselves — `"react"`, `"vue"`, etc. — are identifiers, not translated); on
  `isCancel(result)` → `cancel(t("cancelled"))`, throw `ScaffoldCliError(t("cancelled"), 1)`.
- Directory: same `shouldPrompt` gate; `text({ message: t("promptDir"), placeholder: ".", defaultValue: "." })`
  (clack returns the default on empty Enter, replacing the old manual `.trim() || "."`). Same cancel
  handling.

### `printNextSteps` — package-manager detection, wired in

`detectPackageManager()` parses `process.env.npm_config_user_agent` (the same technique `create-vite`/
`create-vue` use) to get `"npm" | "pnpm" | "yarn" | "bun"`. `printNextSteps` prints a localized
`t("nextStepsInstall", { command: "<detected> install" })` line, falling back to a generic localized
"install dependencies" line when detection fails. This is a real, intentional output change from today's
static English text — three existing test assertions that check for the literal `"vp install"` string need
updating (Phase 5); this is the accepted tradeoff for the more complete "sane defaults" behavior.

### `runScaffoldCli` — the CLI entry point

```ts
export async function runScaffoldCli(argv: string[], options: { usageCommand: string; version?: string }) {
  const program = createScaffoldCommand({
    name: options.usageCommand,
    usageCommand: options.usageCommand,
    version: options.version,
  });
  try {
    await program.parseAsync(argv, { from: "user" });
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof CommanderError) {
      if (err.code === "commander.helpDisplayed" || err.code === "commander.version") return;
      process.exit(err.exitCode);
    }
    if (err instanceof ScaffoldCliError) {
      console.error(err.message);
      process.exit(err.exitCode);
    }
    console.error("Error scaffolding project:", err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

**Own i18n slice**, mirroring Phase 0.5 exactly (same file names, same `translate`/`translate:agy`/
`check:drift` script names, same env vars, own devDependency on `@pantoken/translation-adapters`):
`ai/pantoken-ai/src/i18n.json` (its added strings only — `init`'s description/option text, the `✓ wrote`/
tool-choice error messages it doesn't get from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`), `ai/pantoken-ai/i18n-cache/{en,hu}.json`,
`ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/translate.ts`, `ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/check-drift.ts`, and a `generate.ts` step
writing `ai/pantoken-ai/generated/locales/{en,hu}.ts` + `index.ts`. `ai/pantoken-ai/src/cli.ts` imports
`detectLocale`/`createLocaleLookup` from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli` (reusing the generic lookup/detection
logic, not duplicating it) and builds its own lookup over its own `LOCALES` map — so `pantoken-ai`'s prose
and `@pantoken/scaffold`'s reused prose can both resolve independently to the same detected locale without
either package needing to know about the other's string keys.

**Explicit boundary — what does *not* get localized:** `src/i18n.json` covers only strings the CLI itself
prints to the terminal (`init`/`scaffold`'s own messages). It must **not** include anything from `ASSETS`/
`TARGETS` in `ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts` — `AGENTS_MD`, `LLMS_TXT`, the Cursor/Copilot/Windsurf rule
files, or the `init-pantoken`/`scaffold-pantoken` Claude Code `SKILL.md` files that `installAgentAssets()`
writes into a consumer's repo. Those are content *consumed by AI agents and editor tooling*, not prose read
by a human in their own terminal language, and stay English-only by design — translating agent instruction
files is not this repo's established practice (mirroring how `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts` only ever localizes
short UI chrome, never the API/component reference content itself). Localizing `pantoken-ai init`'s own
*console output* (e.g. `✓ wrote .cursor/rules/pantoken.mdc`) is fine and in scope; localizing the *contents*
of `pantoken.mdc` itself is explicitly out of scope.

New file [ai/pantoken-ai/src/cli.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/src/cli.ts), mirroring the scaffold package's
bin/src split:

```ts
export interface AiCommandOptions { name?: string; version?: string }

export function createAiCommand(options?: AiCommandOptions): Command {
  const program = new Command(options?.name ?? "pantoken-ai")
    .exitOverride()
    .configureOutput({ writeOut: (s) => process.stdout.write(s), writeErr: (s) => process.stderr.write(s) })
    .option("-l, --lang <tag>", "Override the auto-detected display language (e.g. \"hu\")");
  if (options?.version) program.version(options.version, "-v, --version");

  program
    .command("init")
    .description("Write pantoken's agent assets into a repo")
    .addOption(new Option("-t, --tool <tool>", `Tool (${["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS].join("|")})`)
      .default("all").choices(["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS]))
    .option("-d, --dir <path>", "Target directory", ".")
    .action((opts) => {
      const { t } = createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, detectLocale({ langFlag: program.opts().lang }));
      const written = installAgentAssets(opts.tool, opts.dir);
      for (const p of written) console.log(t("wroteFile", { path: p }));
    });

  program
    .command("scaffold")
    .description("Scaffold a starter project (via @pantoken/scaffold) and install agent assets into it")
    .addArgument(new Argument("[platform]", `Platform (${SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS.join("|")})`)
      .argParser(validateScaffoldPlatform))
    .option("-d, --dir <path>", "Target directory (prompts interactively on a TTY if omitted)")
    .option("-y, --yes", "Never prompt", false)
    .addOption(new Option("-t, --tool <tool>", `Agent tool (${["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS].join("|")})`)
      .default("all").choices(["all", ...AGENT_TOOLS]))
    .action(async (platformArg, opts) => {
      const locale = detectLocale({ langFlag: program.opts().lang });
      const { t } = createLocaleLookup(LOCALES, locale); // ai/pantoken-ai's own bundle
      const scaffoldT = createLocaleLookup(SCAFFOLD_LOCALES, locale).t; // @pantoken/scaffold's bundle
      const { platform, dir } = await resolveScaffoldTarget({ platformArg, dirOption: opts.dir, yes: opts.yes, t: scaffoldT });
      const scaffoldFiles = await scaffoldWithSpinner(platform, dir, scaffoldT);
      const assetFiles = installAgentAssets(opts.tool, dir);
      for (const p of [...scaffoldFiles, ...assetFiles]) console.log(t("wroteFile", { path: p }));
      printNextSteps(dir, scaffoldFiles, scaffoldT);
    });

  tab(program, { completionCommandName: "completion" }); // once, on this program's own root
  return program;
}

export async function runAiCli(argv: string[], options?: AiCommandOptions): Promise<void>;
// same exitOverride/CommanderError/ScaffoldCliError catch pattern as runScaffoldCli
```

(`LOCALES` above is `ai/pantoken-ai/generated/locales/index.ts`'s own map; `SCAFFOLD_LOCALES` is
`@pantoken/scaffold/cli`'s `LOCALES` export, imported under a distinct local name to keep the two bundles
visually unambiguous in this file.)

- `resolveScaffoldTarget`, `scaffoldWithSpinner`, `printNextSteps`, `validateScaffoldPlatform`,
  `detectLocale`, `createLocaleLookup` all import from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli` — this is the actual reuse:
  the platform-select/dir-text/spinner UI and its localized copy run unmodified here, then
  `installAgentAssets` runs after with `pantoken-ai`'s own separately-localized strings.
- `scaffold` is built with `.command("scaffold")` + a manually attached `Argument` (not the
  `.command("scaffold <platform>")` shorthand) specifically so `validateScaffoldPlatform` can be attached
  via `.argParser`, keeping one source of truth for the platform-error wording across all three CLIs.
- `printNextSteps` is now shared verbatim, changing `pantoken-ai scaffold`'s output from
  `"\nNext: cd ${dir} && npm install (or pnpm/yarn/bun install)"` to the same "Next steps" block the other
  two CLIs use — a deliberate, user-visible change for `@pantoken/ai`, called out in its changeset entry.
- Completions are wired exactly once, on `ai/pantoken-ai`'s own root `Command` (covers both `init` and
  `scaffold`). `createScaffoldCommand()` is deliberately **not** mounted via `addCommand()` here — reusing
  the granular functions avoids double-registering a nested `completion` subcommand and leaves room for
  the `--tool` option `createScaffoldCommand()` doesn't know about.

## Phase 7 — Changeset

This is a breaking rewrite, not preserved backward compatibility, so all three changesets are `major`. One
changeset file covering all three packages, following the multi-package-changeset precedent of
`.changeset/scaffold-cli-prompt-and-vp-install.md` (from the prior CLI-unification commit `ef503aa0`):

```md
---
"@pantoken/scaffold": major
"create-pantoken-app": major
"@pantoken/ai": major
---

`pantoken-scaffold`, `create-pantoken-app`, and `pantoken-ai` are rebuilt on a shared commander-based CLI
engine (exported from `@pantoken/scaffold/cli`) with proper `--help`, `--version`, and shell completions
(`<command> completion <shell>`). Interactive prompts (platform selection, directory input, a progress
spinner) are now powered by `@clack/prompts` instead of raw `readline`, and CLI prose is localized —
prompts, help text, and messages automatically display in the invoking terminal's language where a
translation exists (starting with English and Hungarian), with a `--lang` flag to override detection and a
graceful fallback to English for any untranslated string. Add a new `--yes`/`-y` flag to force fully
non-interactive behavior for scripts and CI even on a TTY. The post-scaffold "Next steps" message now leads
with your detected package manager's install command instead of a static "vp install" line. `pantoken-ai
scaffold` gains the same platform/directory prompts and localization as the other two CLIs.

**Breaking:** argv error messages, the exact "Next steps" wording, and internal `@alpha`-tagged exports
(e.g. `shouldPromptForDir`, renamed to `shouldPrompt`) have changed. The documented `<platform> [--dir]`
invocation contract for all three commands is unchanged.
```
